title: ser vs estar

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to do or be something is a wish, so the verb after que goes in the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quiero que seas feliz.
examples.en: I want you to be happy.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú) after a wish means que + subjunctive. Never 'quiero que eres'.

examples.es: Quiero que estés tranquila durante la boda.
examples.en: I want you to be calm during the wedding.
examples.note: Estar keeps its written accent in estés, esté and estén. Only estemos has none.

examples.es: Quiero que estés listo a las ocho.
examples.en: I want you to be ready at eight.
examples.note: Listo with estar means ready. 'Seas listo' would mean you should be clever.

contrast.es: Quiero estar listo a las ocho.
contrast.en: I want to be ready at eight.
contrast.note: Same subject means infinitive. A different subject means que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubting or denying something removes the claim of fact, so the subjunctive is needed.

examples.es: No creo que sea caro.
examples.en: I don't think it's expensive.
examples.note: No creo que = doubt, so sea, not es.

examples.es: No creo que Marta esté en casa hoy.
examples.en: I don't think Marta is at home today.
examples.note: Location uses estar, and the subjunctive form esté keeps its accent.

examples.es: No creo que el profesor sea aburrido.
examples.en: I don't think the teacher is boring.
examples.note: With ser, aburrido describes personality. With estar it would mean bored right now.

contrast.es: Creo que el profesor es aburrido.
contrast.en: I think the teacher is boring.
contrast.note: Affirmative creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event that hasn't happened yet takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando estés listo, llámame.
examples.en: When you're ready, call me.
examples.note: The ready moment is still in the future, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando sea mayor, quiero ser piloto.
examples.en: When I grow up, I want to be a pilot.
examples.note: Sea is irregular. It is not 'sía' or 'sera'. Cuando + future idea = subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando estés en Madrid, te enseñaré el barrio.
examples.en: When you're in Madrid, I'll show you the neighbourhood.
examples.note: One future visit that hasn't happened yet, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando estás en Madrid, te enseño el barrio.
contrast.en: Whenever you're in Madrid, I show you the neighbourhood.
contrast.note: A habit or fact uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Sea is ser and esté is estar, never the other way round: 'espero que estés bien', not 'espero que seas bien'. Estar keeps the accent in estés, esté and estén (but not estemos), and 'o sea' is just 'I mean', not a subjunctive clause.

title: fue vs era

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, which is not a fact, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá sea una noche tranquila.
examples.en: I hope it's a quiet night.
examples.note: After ojalá, a hope about the present or future uses sea. Fue and era can't follow it.

examples.es: Ojalá el concierto sea tan bueno como dicen.
examples.en: I hope the concert is as good as they say.
examples.note: Ojalá + present subjunctive = hope about what's still to come.

examples.es: Ojalá la entrevista sea corta.
examples.en: I hope the interview is short.
examples.note: You are hoping about something that hasn't happened yet.

contrast.es: La entrevista fue corta.
contrast.en: The interview was short.
contrast.note: Fue states a completed fact. After ojalá, sea expresses a hope.

triggers.explanation: Denying that something is true means you aren't asserting it as fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No es cierto que sea caro.
examples.en: It's not true that it's expensive.
examples.note: Denial = subjunctive. The ser form is sea.

examples.es: No es cierto que la fiesta sea mañana.
examples.en: It's not true that the party is tomorrow.
examples.note: Events use ser, and the denial pushes it into the subjunctive.

examples.es: No es cierto que él sea mi mejor amigo.
examples.en: It's not true that he's my best friend.
examples.note: You deny the present state. Era or fue would put it in the past.

contrast.es: Es cierto que fue mi mejor amigo.
contrast.en: It's true that he was my best friend.
contrast.note: Es cierto states a fact (indicative, and fue = the friendship is over). No es cierto denies it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something uncertain or hypothetical.

examples.es: Aunque sea tarde, voy a ir.
examples.en: Even if it's late, I'm going to go.
examples.note: Sea means even if it turns out to be late. The fact isn't established.

examples.es: Aunque la entrevista sea larga, no te preocupes.
examples.en: Even if the interview is long, don't worry.
examples.note: You don't know yet how long it will be, so aunque + subjunctive.

examples.es: Aunque sea difícil, lo haré.
examples.en: Even if it's hard, I'll do it.
examples.note: You are allowing for the possibility that it's hard.

contrast.es: Aunque fue difícil, lo hice.
contrast.en: Although it was hard, I did it.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact (fue = completed past). Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: The present subjunctive of ser is sea, seas, sean, so fue and era never appear after these triggers. Watch fuera and fuese: they look like fue and era but are the imperfect subjunctive, for 'ojalá fuera' (I wish it were). Aunque + sea is hypothetical, aunque + fue is a fact.

title: por vs para

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose involving a different subject, which is an unrealised goal, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Trabajo para que mi familia viva bien.
examples.en: I work so my family can live well.
examples.note: Para que + subjunctive when the person doing the second action is different.

examples.es: Te llamo para que me digas la verdad.
examples.en: I'm calling you so that you'll tell me the truth.
examples.note: Decir is irregular: digas, not 'dices' or 'decías'.

examples.es: Te escribo para que sepas que pienso en ti.
examples.en: I'm writing so that you know I'm thinking of you.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú) = para que + subjunctive.

contrast.es: Te escribo para saber cómo estás.
contrast.en: I'm writing to find out how you are.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. Different subject = para que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Necessity is a judgement about what should happen, not a fact, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es necesario que hablemos por teléfono.
examples.en: We need to talk by phone.
examples.note: Por teléfono = by means of the phone. Es necesario que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Es necesario que pagues por adelantado.
examples.en: You need to pay in advance.
examples.note: Pagar needs gu before e: pagues, never 'pages'.

examples.es: Es necesario que lo hagas por convicción, no por obligación.
examples.en: You have to do it out of conviction, not out of obligation.
examples.note: Por = motive or cause. Hacer is irregular: hagas.

contrast.es: Es necesario hacerlo por convicción.
contrast.en: It's necessary to do it out of conviction.
contrast.note: No specific person = infinitive. Naming who must act = que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubt means you don't take the statement as fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudo que Ana trabaje por la noche.
examples.en: I doubt Ana works at night.
examples.note: Por la noche = during the night (por for time periods).

examples.es: Dudo que lleguen para las ocho.
examples.en: I doubt they'll arrive by eight.
examples.note: Llegar needs gu before e: lleguen. Para = a deadline.

examples.es: Dudo que este regalo sea para mí.
examples.en: I doubt this gift is for me.
examples.note: Para marks the recipient.

contrast.es: No dudo que este regalo es para mí.
contrast.en: I don't doubt this gift is for me.
contrast.note: Dudar takes the subjunctive. No dudar expresses certainty, so the indicative.

tricky: Por and para never change, but 'para que' always forces the subjunctive. It is not the same as 'porque' (because), which takes the indicative. With the same subject use para + infinitive: 'Estudio para aprobar', not 'para que apruebe'.

title: saber vs conocer

triggers.explanation: When you describe someone who may not exist or isn't identified, the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Busco a alguien que sepa cocinar.
examples.en: I'm looking for someone who knows how to cook.
examples.note: Saber = skill. Sepa is irregular, not 'sabe'.

examples.es: Busco a alguien que conozca la ciudad.
examples.en: I'm looking for someone who knows the city.
examples.note: Conocer adds -zc-: conozca, never 'conosca'. Conocer = to be familiar with a place.

examples.es: Busco a alguien que conozca a mi hermano.
examples.en: I'm looking for someone who knows my brother.
examples.note: Any person who fits, existence not guaranteed, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Busco a la chica que conoce a mi hermano.
contrast.en: I'm looking for the girl who knows my brother.
contrast.note: A specific, known person takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Antes de que refers to something that hasn't happened yet, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dímelo antes de que lo sepan todos.
examples.en: Tell me before everyone knows.
examples.note: Antes de que always triggers the subjunctive. Sepan is the ellos form of saber.

examples.es: Te lo explico antes de que conozcas a mi familia.
examples.en: I'll explain it to you before you meet my family.
examples.note: Conocer = to meet someone for the first time.

examples.es: Cuéntaselo antes de que lo sepa por otra persona.
examples.en: Tell her before she finds out from someone else.
examples.note: Antes de que + subjunctive: the knowing hasn't happened yet.

contrast.es: Se lo conté después de que lo supo por otra persona.
contrast.en: I told her after she found out from someone else.
contrast.note: Después de que with a completed event takes the indicative, while antes de que always takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Reacting emotionally to something takes the subjunctive, even when the fact is true.

examples.es: Me alegro de que conozcas a Sofía.
examples.en: I'm glad you're meeting Sofía.
examples.note: Emotion + different subject = que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Me alegro de que sepas tanto de música.
examples.en: I'm glad you know so much about music.
examples.note: Saber de = to know about a subject. Sepas is irregular.

examples.es: Me alegro de que ya conozcas a mi jefe.
examples.en: I'm glad you already know my boss.
examples.note: Conocer is personal acquaintance.

contrast.es: Sé que ya conoces a mi jefe.
contrast.en: I know you already know my boss.
contrast.note: Simply knowing a fact takes the indicative. Reacting to it takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Sepa (saber) is irregular and conozca (conocer) takes -zc-, so 'conozca', never 'conosca'. With 'busco a alguien que...', 'que sepa' means anyone who qualifies, while 'que sabe' points to a particular person you already have in mind.

title: salir vs quedar

triggers.explanation: Hoping for something involves a wish, not a fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Espero que quedemos el sábado.
examples.en: I hope we get together on Saturday.
examples.note: Quedar = to arrange to meet. Quedemos is the nosotros subjunctive.

examples.es: Espero que salgas con nosotros esta noche.
examples.en: I hope you'll go out with us tonight.
examples.note: Salir is irregular: salgas, with a -g-.

examples.es: Espero que la cena de mañana salga bien.
examples.en: I hope tomorrow's dinner goes well.
examples.note: Salir bien = to turn out well. Hope = subjunctive.

contrast.es: Sé que la cena de mañana saldrá bien.
contrast.en: I know tomorrow's dinner will go well.
contrast.note: Saber = certainty, so indicative. Esperar = hope, so subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Saying what would be better is a judgement, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es mejor que quedemos en el centro.
examples.en: It's better if we meet downtown.
examples.note: Quedar en = to arrange to meet at a place. In Spain, el centro (the city centre).

examples.es: Es mejor que salgas temprano del trabajo.
examples.en: It's better if you leave work early.
examples.note: Salir de = to leave a place. Salgas has a -g-.

examples.es: Es mejor que no salgas esta noche.
examples.en: It's better that you don't go out tonight.
examples.note: Advice, not fact, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Es obvio que no sales esta noche.
contrast.en: It's obvious you're not going out tonight.
contrast.note: Es obvio states a fact (indicative). Es mejor gives advice (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Hasta que about something not yet completed takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Trabajo hasta que salga el último cliente.
examples.en: I work until the last customer leaves.
examples.note: The leaving hasn't happened yet, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No te vayas hasta que quede todo limpio.
examples.en: Don't leave until everything is clean.
examples.note: Quedar + adjective = to end up / be left in a state.

examples.es: Voy a esperar hasta que salgas del hospital.
examples.en: I'm going to wait until you leave the hospital.
examples.note: Future / unfinished event = subjunctive.

contrast.es: Esperé hasta que saliste del hospital.
contrast.en: I waited until you left the hospital.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Quedar is a chameleon: quedar con alguien (to arrange to meet), quedar (to be left, to fit) and quedarse (to stay). Its subjunctive is regular (quede, quedemos), but salir is not: salga, salgas, salgamos, with a -g-, like tener and poner.

title: llevar vs hacer (time)

triggers.explanation: Reacting with surprise to a fact calls for the subjunctive, even though the fact is true.

examples.es: Me sorprende que lleves tanto tiempo esperando.
examples.en: I'm surprised you've been waiting for so long.
examples.note: Llevar + gerund = how long you've been doing something. Lleves is the tú subjunctive.

examples.es: Me sorprende que haga tantos años que no nos vemos.
examples.en: I'm surprised it's been so many years since we last saw each other.
examples.note: Hace + time becomes haga. The clause after que stays indicative: nos vemos.

examples.es: Me sorprende que Ana lleve diez años sin vacaciones.
examples.en: I'm surprised Ana has gone ten years without a holiday.
examples.note: Llevar + time + sin + noun = how long you've gone without something.

contrast.es: Sé que Ana lleva diez años sin vacaciones.
contrast.en: I know Ana has gone ten years without a holiday.
contrast.note: Simply knowing a fact takes the indicative. Reacting to it takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que lleve mucho tiempo.
examples.en: I don't think it takes long.
examples.note: Llevar can also mean to take (time).

examples.es: No creo que haga ya un año que se marchó.
examples.en: I don't think it's been a year already since he left.
examples.note: Only hace changes: hace un año que se marchó becomes haga un año que se marchó. Haga is irregular.

examples.es: No creo que lleven aquí más de una semana.
examples.en: I don't think they've been here more than a week.
examples.note: Lleven aquí + time = how long they've been here.

contrast.es: Creo que llevan aquí más de una semana.
contrast.en: I think they've been here more than a week.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about a future event that hasn't happened yet takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto lleve el coche al taller, te llamo.
examples.en: As soon as I take the car to the garage, I'll call you.
examples.note: The taking hasn't happened yet, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto haga calor, iremos a la playa.
examples.en: As soon as it's warm, we'll go to the beach.
examples.note: Weather uses hacer: hace calor becomes haga calor.

examples.es: En cuanto lleves un año aquí, podrás pedir el permiso.
examples.en: As soon as you've been here a year, you'll be able to apply for the permit.
examples.note: A time threshold that hasn't been reached yet, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: En cuanto llevas un año aquí, puedes pedir el permiso.
contrast.en: As soon as you've been here a year, you can apply for the permit.
contrast.note: A general rule that always applies uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Llevar is regular (lleve, lleves) and hacer is irregular (haga, hagas), so never 'haca'. In hace-clauses only 'hace' changes: 'Es increíble que haga diez años que vivo aquí', where the second clause stays indicative. Llevar + gerund keeps the gerund: 'no creo que lleve dos años viviendo aquí'.

title: pedir vs preguntar

triggers.explanation: A command passed on through que is a wish for someone to act, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dile que pregunte por el horario.
examples.en: Tell him to ask about the schedule.
examples.note: Preguntar por = to ask about / ask after. Regular: pregunte.

examples.es: Dile que pida un café con leche.
examples.en: Tell him to order a coffee with milk.
examples.note: Pedir changes e→i in the subjunctive: pida, not 'peda'. Pedir = to ask for / order.

examples.es: Dile que pida perdón a su madre.
examples.en: Tell him to apologise to his mother.
examples.note: Pedir perdón = to apologise. Dile que = an instruction.

contrast.es: Dice que pide perdón a su madre.
contrast.en: He says he apologises to his mother.
contrast.note: Dile que gives an order, so the subjunctive. Dice que reports a fact, so the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Annoyance is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive follows.

examples.es: Me molesta que preguntes tantas cosas.
examples.en: It annoys me that you ask so many questions.
examples.note: Regular verb, regular -es ending.

examples.es: Me molesta que siempre pidas lo más caro.
examples.en: It bothers me that you always order the most expensive thing.
examples.note: Stem change e→i: pidas.

examples.es: Me molesta que nunca me preguntes cómo estoy.
examples.en: It bothers me that you never ask me how I am.
examples.note: Preguntar = ask a question. 'Me pidas cómo estoy' would be wrong.

contrast.es: Nunca me preguntas cómo estoy.
contrast.en: You never ask me how I am.
contrast.note: A plain statement uses the indicative. The emotional reaction uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Sin que always takes the subjunctive when a different subject is involved.

examples.es: Entra sin que nadie pregunte nada.
examples.en: He goes in without anyone asking anything.
examples.note: Sin que = without + a different subject.

examples.es: Lo hace todo sin que se lo pidan.
examples.en: She does everything without being asked.
examples.note: Stem change in the ellos form: pidan.

examples.es: Voy a entrar sin que me pidan el carné.
examples.en: I'm going to get in without them asking for my ID.
examples.note: They ask, I get in, so a different subject.

contrast.es: Voy a entrar sin pedir el carné.
contrast.en: I'm going to go in without asking for the ID.
contrast.note: Same subject = sin + infinitive. Different subject = sin que + subjunctive.

tricky: Pedir changes its stem e→i in every present-subjunctive form, nosotros included: pida, pidas, pida, pidamos, pidan, never 'pedamos'. Preguntar is regular: pregunte. Keep the meanings apart too: 'que pregunte por ti' asks a question about you, while 'que pida por ti' would mean ask on your behalf.

title: poder vs saber (can)

triggers.explanation: A mere possibility isn't a fact, so the subjunctive is used.

examples.es: Es posible que Luis pueda venir mañana.
examples.en: It's possible that Luis can come tomorrow.
examples.note: Poder = be able to / have the chance. Pueda has the o→ue stem change.

examples.es: Es posible que mañana no podamos salir.
examples.en: It's possible we won't be able to go out tomorrow.
examples.note: Nosotros keeps o: podamos, never 'puedamos'.

examples.es: Es posible que él no sepa nadar.
examples.en: It's possible he can't swim.
examples.note: Saber + infinitive = can, as a learned skill. Sepa is irregular.

contrast.es: Es evidente que él no sabe nadar.
contrast.en: It's obvious he can't swim.
contrast.note: Es posible expresses uncertainty (subjunctive). Es evidente states a fact (indicative).

triggers.explanation: Strong liking or delight is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive follows.

examples.es: Me encanta que sepas cantar.
examples.en: I love that you can sing.
examples.note: Saber cantar = can sing as a skill. Sepas is irregular.

examples.es: Me encanta que puedan venir todos.
examples.en: I love that everyone can come.
examples.note: Poder = be free / able to. O→ue stem: puedan.

examples.es: Me encanta que sepas tocar el piano.
examples.en: I love that you can play the piano.
examples.note: A skill you learned uses saber, not poder.

contrast.es: Veo que sabes tocar el piano.
contrast.en: I see you can play the piano.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting emotionally uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: A menos que always takes the subjunctive because it introduces a condition that may not happen.

examples.es: Iré a la fiesta a menos que no pueda.
examples.en: I'll go to the party unless I can't.
examples.note: A menos que = unless. Always followed by the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te ayudo a menos que no sepa cómo hacerlo.
examples.en: I'll help you unless I don't know how to do it.
examples.note: Saber cómo = to know how to.

examples.es: No iré a menos que pueda llevar a mi hijo.
examples.en: I won't go unless I can take my son.
examples.note: Poder = to be allowed / able.

contrast.es: No iré si no puedo llevar a mi hijo.
contrast.en: I won't go if I can't take my son.
contrast.note: Si + present indicative expresses a similar condition. A menos que always needs the subjunctive.

tricky: Poder has a stem change o→ue in all forms except nosotros: pueda, puedas, puedan, but podamos, never 'puedamos'. Saber's subjunctive is sepa, irregular. And for 'can', poder is ability or permission today, while saber + infinitive is a learned skill: 'que sepas nadar' (you know how), 'que puedas nadar' (you're able to, e.g. today).

title: deber vs tener que

triggers.explanation: Judging what is normal is an evaluation, not a statement of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es normal que tengas miedo.
examples.en: It's normal that you're scared.
examples.note: Tener miedo = to be afraid. Tengas is irregular, with a -g-.

examples.es: Es normal que tengamos que repetir los ejercicios.
examples.en: It's normal that we have to repeat the exercises.
examples.note: Tener que + infinitive = have to. Tener changes (tengamos), but tener que doesn't change.

examples.es: Es normal que deba de estar cansada.
examples.en: It's normal that she must be tired.
examples.note: Deber de + infinitive = probability. Here deba is the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Debe de estar cansada.
contrast.en: She must be tired.
contrast.note: Deber de = probability. Deber + infinitive without de = obligation.

triggers.explanation: Fear is an emotion, and the thing feared hasn't happened, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Temo que tengas razón.
examples.en: I'm afraid you're right.
examples.note: Tener razón = to be right. Temo que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Temo que debas pagar una multa.
examples.en: I'm afraid you have to pay a fine.
examples.note: Deber + infinitive = must / have to. It's regular: debas.

examples.es: Temo que tengan que cancelar el viaje.
examples.en: I fear they'll have to cancel the trip.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / ellos) = que + subjunctive.

contrast.es: Sé que tienen que cancelar el viaje.
contrast.en: I know they have to cancel the trip.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Temo que expresses fear (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Por mucho que means 'however much', and it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Por mucho que tengas, nunca es suficiente.
examples.en: However much you have, it's never enough.
examples.note: Por mucho que + subjunctive = however much.

examples.es: Por mucho que deba estudiar, siempre saca tiempo para jugar.
examples.en: However much he has to study, he always finds time to play.
examples.note: Deber + infinitive = obligation. Deba is regular.

examples.es: Por mucho que tengas que esforzarte, vale la pena.
examples.en: However hard you have to try, it's worth it.
examples.note: Concession with a hypothetical amount of effort.

contrast.es: Tienes que esforzarte mucho, pero vale la pena.
contrast.en: You have to try very hard, but it's worth it.
contrast.note: A flat statement of fact uses the indicative. Por mucho que + subjunctive concedes a point.

tricky: Tener has irregular -g- forms (tenga, tengamos), but deber is regular (deba, debamos). Watch the two verbs together: in 'es normal que tengamos que repetirlo' only tener changes, and tener que is still followed by an infinitive. Deber de + infinitive means probability, not obligation.

title: ir vs venir

triggers.explanation: Asking someone to do something is a request, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te pido que vengas temprano.
examples.en: I ask you to come early.
examples.note: Venir is irregular: vengas, with a -g-, like tener.

examples.es: Te pido que vayas a la farmacia.
examples.en: I'm asking you to go to the pharmacy.
examples.note: Ir is irregular in the subjunctive: vayas. And 'ya voy' = I'm coming to you.

examples.es: Te pido que vengas conmigo al médico.
examples.en: I'm asking you to come with me to the doctor.
examples.note: Venir = movement toward the speaker or a shared destination.

contrast.es: Me dices que vienes conmigo al médico.
contrast.en: You tell me you're coming with me to the doctor.
contrast.note: Pedir que = a request (subjunctive). Decir que = reporting (indicative).

triggers.explanation: Después de que about an event that hasn't happened yet takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Salgo después de que venga mi madre.
examples.en: I go out after my mother comes.
examples.note: The coming hasn't happened yet, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Comemos después de que vayamos al banco.
examples.en: We'll eat after we go to the bank.
examples.note: Vayamos is the nosotros subjunctive. 'Vamos' means 'let's go' or 'we go'.

examples.es: Hablamos después de que vengas a casa.
examples.en: We'll talk after you come home.
examples.note: Future / not yet happened, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Hablamos después de que viniste a casa.
contrast.en: We talked after you came home.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Judging something as strange is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es raro que Luis no venga.
examples.en: It's odd that Luis isn't coming.
examples.note: Es raro que + subjunctive, even though the fact is real.

examples.es: Es raro que vayan solos.
examples.en: It's odd that they're going on their own.
examples.note: Vayan is the ellos form of ir.

examples.es: Es raro que no vengas a las reuniones.
examples.en: It's odd that you don't come to the meetings.
examples.note: The speaker is evaluating a fact, not stating one.

contrast.es: Es cierto que no vienes a las reuniones.
contrast.en: It's true that you don't come to the meetings.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es raro judges it (subjunctive).

tricky: Ir's present subjunctive is vaya, vayas, vaya, vayamos, vayan, never 'vaye'. Venir is irregular (venga, vengas), like tener. 'Let's go' is 'vamos' (not 'vayamos'), while the negative is 'no vayamos'. And in Spanish you say 'Ya voy' (I'm coming) because ir follows the other person's location.

title: traer vs llevar

triggers.explanation: Needing someone else to act is a request, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Necesito que lleves esta carta al correo.
examples.en: I need you to take this letter to the post office.
examples.note: Llevar = to take away from where we are. Regular: lleves.

examples.es: Necesito que me traigas los documentos.
examples.en: I need you to bring me the documents.
examples.note: Traer is irregular: traigas, with -ig-, like traigo.

examples.es: Necesito que traigas los papeles a la oficina.
examples.en: I need you to bring the papers to the office.
examples.note: Traer = toward the speaker's location. The office is where I am.

contrast.es: Necesito traer los papeles a la oficina.
contrast.en: I need to bring the papers to the office.
contrast.note: Same person = infinitive. A different person = que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Calling something important is a judgement about what should happen, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es importante que lleves agua.
examples.en: It's important that you take water.
examples.note: Regular: lleves.

examples.es: Es importante que todos traigan el pasaporte.
examples.en: It's important that everyone brings their passport.
examples.note: Todos is plural, so traigan.

examples.es: Es importante que lleves el paraguas hoy.
examples.en: It's important that you take the umbrella today.
examples.note: Llevar here means carry with you.

contrast.es: Es evidente que llevas el paraguas hoy.
contrast.en: It's obvious you're carrying the umbrella today.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es importante expresses what should happen (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Con tal de que introduces a condition that may or may not be met, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Voy a la fiesta con tal de que me lleves.
examples.en: I'll go to the party as long as you take me.
examples.note: Con tal de que always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te presto el coche con tal de que lo traigas con el depósito lleno.
examples.en: I'll lend you the car as long as you bring it back with a full tank.
examples.note: Traer = bring back to where I am.

examples.es: Hago lo que sea con tal de que me traigan buenas noticias.
examples.en: I'll do anything as long as they bring me good news.
examples.note: A different subject, so con tal de que + subjunctive.

contrast.es: Hago lo que sea con tal de traer buenas noticias.
contrast.en: I'll do anything to bring good news.
contrast.note: Same subject = con tal de + infinitive. Different subject = con tal de que + subjunctive.

tricky: Traer is irregular: traiga, traigas, traigamos, traigan (the -ig- of traigo carries through). Llevar is regular: lleve. Direction decides the verb: 'que me traigas' (bring it to me) vs 'que me lleves' (take me away).

title: querer vs amar

triggers.explanation: Preferring that someone else act in a certain way is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Prefiero que ames tu trabajo.
examples.en: I'd prefer you to love your job.
examples.note: Amar is regular: ames.

examples.es: Prefiero que me quieras tal como soy.
examples.en: I'd prefer that you love me as I am.
examples.note: Querer has an e→ie stem change: quieras, not 'quereas'.

examples.es: Prefiero que quieran a mis hijos como a los suyos.
examples.en: I'd prefer that they love my children like their own.
examples.note: Querer a = to love someone (family, friends). The personal a is needed.

contrast.es: Sé que quieren a mis hijos como a los suyos.
contrast.en: I know they love my children like their own.
contrast.note: Saber states a fact (indicative). Preferir expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Tal vez expresses real uncertainty, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Tal vez ame la música clásica.
examples.en: Maybe he loves classical music.
examples.note: Tal vez + subjunctive = genuine doubt.

examples.es: Tal vez quiera quedarse en casa.
examples.en: Maybe she wants to stay at home.
examples.note: Querer = to want. The e→ie stem change: quiera.

examples.es: Tal vez quiera a su ex todavía.
examples.en: Maybe she still loves her ex.
examples.note: You aren't sure, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Tal vez quiere a su ex todavía.
contrast.en: Maybe she still loves her ex (I lean toward yes).
contrast.note: Tal vez + indicative is also possible and leans toward belief. The subjunctive signals stronger doubt.

triggers.explanation: Por más que means 'no matter how much', and it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Por más que quiera, no puedo ir.
examples.en: No matter how much I want to, I can't go.
examples.note: Por más que + subjunctive = however much.

examples.es: Por más que ames tu trabajo, necesitas vacaciones.
examples.en: No matter how much you love your job, you need a holiday.
examples.note: Concession with a hypothetical degree.

examples.es: Por más que lo quieras, no cambiará.
examples.en: No matter how much you love him, he won't change.
examples.note: Lo quieras = you love him. Concession.

contrast.es: Lo quieres mucho, pero no cambiará.
contrast.en: You love him a lot, but he won't change.
contrast.note: A direct statement of fact uses the indicative. Por más que + subjunctive concedes a point.

tricky: Querer changes its stem (e→ie) in every form except nosotros: quiera, quieras, quieran, but queramos, never 'quieramos'. Amar is regular (ame). Querer a + person is the everyday word for love, while 'querer que' means want. Amar sounds stronger, more romantic or poetic.

title: mirar vs ver

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quiero que mires esta foto.
examples.en: I want you to look at this photo.
examples.note: Mirar is regular: mires.

examples.es: Quiero que veas esta película conmigo.
examples.en: I want you to see this film with me.
examples.note: Ver is irregular in the subjunctive: veas, not 'ves'.

examples.es: Quiero que me mires a los ojos.
examples.en: I want you to look me in the eye.
examples.note: Mirar = point your eyes deliberately.

contrast.es: Quiero mirarte a los ojos.
contrast.en: I want to look you in the eye.
contrast.note: Same subject = infinitive. A different subject = que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Likelihood isn't certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es probable que mire la tele esta noche.
examples.en: I'll probably watch TV tonight.
examples.note: Mirar la tele = to watch TV (deliberately looking).

examples.es: Es probable que veamos a tus primos mañana.
examples.en: We'll probably see your cousins tomorrow.
examples.note: Veamos is the nosotros form. It also means 'let's see'.

examples.es: Es probable que vea a Marta en la fiesta.
examples.en: I'll probably see Marta at the party.
examples.note: Ver = to see or run into, without effort.

contrast.es: Seguro que veo a Marta en la fiesta.
contrast.en: I'm sure I'll see Marta at the party.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Es probable que = likelihood (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: When the person you describe doesn't exist, the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: No hay nadie que mire esa serie.
examples.en: There's nobody who watches that series.
examples.note: Nadie = no such person, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No hay nadie que vea bien sin gafas.
examples.en: There's nobody who sees well without glasses.
examples.note: Vea = ver.

examples.es: No hay nadie que vea el error.
examples.en: There's nobody who sees the error.
examples.note: A non-existent person calls for the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Hay alguien que ve el error.
contrast.en: There is someone who sees the error.
contrast.note: Hay alguien que + indicative: such a person exists.

tricky: Ver's present subjunctive is vea, veas, veamos, vean, never 'vee'. Veamos does double duty as 'let's see', a subjunctive used as a command, while vemos is 'we see'. Mirar is regular (mire). Mirar is the deliberate act, ver is what reaches your eyes.

title: escuchar vs oír

triggers.explanation: Giving advice expresses what you want someone to do, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te aconsejo que escuches a tu madre.
examples.en: I advise you to listen to your mother.
examples.note: Escuchar is regular: escuches.

examples.es: Te aconsejo que oigas ambas versiones.
examples.en: I advise you to hear both versions.
examples.note: Oír is irregular: oigas, with a -g-.

examples.es: Te aconsejo que escuches lo que dice el médico.
examples.en: I advise you to listen to what the doctor says.
examples.note: Escuchar = listen with attention.

contrast.es: Te digo que escuchas lo que dice el médico.
contrast.en: I'm telling you that you listen to what the doctor says.
contrast.note: Aconsejar expresses a wish (subjunctive). Decir que reports a fact (indicative).

triggers.explanation: Expressing regret is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es una lástima que no escuches música.
examples.en: It's a shame you don't listen to music.
examples.note: Es una lástima que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Es una lástima que no oigan bien.
examples.en: It's a shame they can't hear well.
examples.note: Oír is the ability to hear. Oigan has a -g-.

examples.es: Es una lástima que no oigas bien con ese ruido.
examples.en: It's a shame you can't hear well with that noise.
examples.note: Oír = physically hear, not choose to.

contrast.es: Es cierto que no oyes bien con ese ruido.
contrast.en: It's true that you can't hear well with that noise.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es una lástima reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hablo alto para que todos escuchen.
examples.en: I speak loudly so that everyone listens.
examples.note: Para que = so that. Different subjects.

examples.es: Te lo repito para que lo oigas bien.
examples.en: I'm repeating it so that you hear it properly.
examples.note: Oír = to catch what is said.

examples.es: Pon la radio para que escuchemos las noticias.
examples.en: Put the radio on so that we can listen to the news.
examples.note: Different subjects (tú / nosotros).

contrast.es: Pon la radio para escuchar las noticias.
contrast.en: Put the radio on to listen to the news.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. Different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Oír has a -g- in the subjunctive: oiga, oigas, oigamos, oigan, never 'oya' or 'oye'. 'Oiga' is also the formal way to get attention ('excuse me!'), the same form. Escuchar is regular: escuche. Don't mix them: 'que oigas' is the sound reaching you, 'que escuches' is you paying attention.

title: acordarse vs recordar

triggers.explanation: Expressing amazement is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es increíble que te acuerdes de todo.
examples.en: It's incredible that you remember everything.
examples.note: Acordarse de = to remember. O→ue stem: te acuerdes.

examples.es: Es increíble que recuerden aquel día.
examples.en: It's incredible that they remember that day.
examples.note: Recordar takes no de. O→ue stem: recuerden.

examples.es: Es increíble que no te acuerdes de mi cumpleaños.
examples.en: It's incredible that you don't remember my birthday.
examples.note: Acordarse is reflexive and takes de.

contrast.es: Es cierto que no te acuerdas de mi cumpleaños.
contrast.en: It's true that you don't remember my birthday.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es increíble reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: No es que denies a reason someone might assume, and takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: No es que me acuerde de todo.
examples.en: It's not that I remember everything.
examples.note: Reflexive: me acuerde.

examples.es: No es que recuerde mucho de aquella época.
examples.en: It's not that I remember much from that time.
examples.note: Recordar + direct object, no de.

examples.es: No es que me acuerde mal; es que nadie me lo dijo.
examples.en: It's not that I remember badly; it's that nobody told me.
examples.note: You are denying a reason.

contrast.es: Es que me acuerdo mal.
contrast.en: The thing is, I have a bad memory.
contrast.note: Es que + indicative gives a real reason. No es que + subjunctive denies one.

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto te acuerdes, avísame.
examples.en: As soon as you remember, let me know.
examples.note: The remembering hasn't happened yet.

examples.es: En cuanto recuerde su nombre, te lo digo.
examples.en: As soon as I remember his name, I'll tell you.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto me acuerde, te llamo.
examples.en: As soon as I remember, I'll call you.
examples.note: A future moment that hasn't come yet.

contrast.es: En cuanto me acuerdo, te llamo.
contrast.en: Whenever I remember, I call you.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Acordarse takes de ('me acuerdo de eso') while recordar takes the object directly ('recuerdo eso'). Both have the o→ue stem change (me acuerde, recuerde) except nosotros (nos acordemos, recordemos). Only recordar can mean 'to remind': 'Recuérdame que...'.

title: sentir vs sentirse

triggers.explanation: Hoping something for someone else is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Espero que te sientas mejor.
examples.en: I hope you feel better.
examples.note: Sentirse + adjective = to feel (a state). Reflexive: te sientas.

examples.es: Espero que nos sintamos cómodos aquí.
examples.en: I hope we feel comfortable here.
examples.note: Nosotros shows e→i: sintamos, not 'sentamos'.

examples.es: Espero que no te sientas obligado.
examples.en: I hope you don't feel obliged.
examples.note: Sentirse obligado = to feel obliged. The reflexive describes your own state.

contrast.es: Sé que no te sientes obligado.
contrast.en: I know you don't feel obliged.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Espero que expresses a hope (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Regret is an emotional reaction to something, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Lamento que te sientas solo.
examples.en: I'm sorry you feel lonely.
examples.note: Sentirse solo = to feel lonely.

examples.es: Lamento que sientas tanto dolor.
examples.en: I'm sorry you feel so much pain.
examples.note: Sentir + noun = to feel something. No reflexive pronoun.

examples.es: Lamento que se sienta culpable.
examples.en: I'm sorry he feels guilty.
examples.note: Sentirse culpable = to feel guilty. Reflexive.

contrast.es: Veo que se siente culpable.
contrast.en: I see he feels guilty.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something not established as true.

examples.es: Aunque me sienta mal, iré.
examples.en: Even if I feel bad, I'll go.
examples.note: Hypothetical feeling, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Aunque sienta miedo, seguiré adelante.
examples.en: Even if I feel fear, I'll carry on.
examples.note: Sentir miedo = to feel fear. No reflexive pronoun.

examples.es: Aunque te sientas cansado, tienes que ir.
examples.en: Even if you feel tired, you have to go.
examples.note: You aren't sure you'll feel tired, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Aunque te sientes cansado, tienes que ir.
contrast.en: Although you do feel tired, you have to go.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = the tiredness is real. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Sentir has a double stem change: sienta, sientas, sientan, but sintamos (e→i in nosotros). Watch the homonym: 'que te sientas' is sentirse (you feel), yet 'tú te sientas' is also sentarse (you sit). Without the reflexive it's a different meaning: 'que sientas pena' (feel sorrow) vs 'que te sientas triste' (feel sad).

title: pensar vs creer

triggers.explanation: Denying that something is true removes it from fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No es verdad que piense en otra persona.
examples.en: It's not true that I'm thinking of someone else.
examples.note: Pensar en = to think about. E→ie stem: piense.

examples.es: No es verdad que ella crea en fantasmas.
examples.en: It's not true that she believes in ghosts.
examples.note: Creer en = to believe in. Crea is regular.

examples.es: No es verdad que él crea todo lo que dicen.
examples.en: It's not true that he believes everything they say.
examples.note: Creer = to believe something is true.

contrast.es: Es verdad que él cree todo lo que dicen.
contrast.en: It's true that he believes everything they say.
contrast.note: Es verdad asserts a fact (indicative). No es verdad denies it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Fear is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me da miedo que pienses mal de mí.
examples.en: I'm afraid you'll think badly of me.
examples.note: Pensar mal de = to think badly of.

examples.es: Me da miedo que no crean mi historia.
examples.en: I'm afraid they won't believe my story.
examples.note: Creer + direct object = to believe.

examples.es: Me da miedo que piensen que miento.
examples.en: I'm afraid they'll think I'm lying.
examples.note: Pensar que + indicative: 'miento' stays indicative.

contrast.es: Sé que piensan que miento.
contrast.en: I know they think I'm lying.
contrast.note: Sé que takes the indicative. Me da miedo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto piense en algo, te aviso.
examples.en: As soon as I think of something, I'll let you know.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto crea que está listo, te lo digo.
examples.en: As soon as I think it's ready, I'll tell you.
examples.note: Creer que + indicative: 'está listo' is indicative.

examples.es: En cuanto lo piense bien, decidiré.
examples.en: As soon as I've thought it through, I'll decide.
examples.note: Pensar bien = to think carefully.

contrast.es: En cuanto lo pienso bien, decido.
contrast.en: As soon as I think it through, I decide.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Creo que and pienso que take the indicative, but no creo que and no pienso que take the subjunctive. Pensar has an e→ie stem change (piense, pienses, piensen) but pensemos in nosotros. Creer is regular but the double e disappears: cree (indicative) becomes crea (subjunctive).

title: gastar vs pasar (spend)

triggers.explanation: Not wanting something to happen is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No quiero que gastes tanto dinero.
examples.en: I don't want you to spend so much money.
examples.note: Gastar = spend money or use up. Regular.

examples.es: No quiero que pases la noche solo.
examples.en: I don't want you to spend the night alone.
examples.note: Pasar = spend time, never gastar.

examples.es: No quiero que se gaste la vida trabajando.
examples.en: I don't want him to wear his life away working.
examples.note: Gastarse la vida = to wear your life away. Gastarse is reflexive here.

contrast.es: No quiero gastarme la vida trabajando.
contrast.en: I don't want to spend my whole life working.
contrast.note: Same subject = infinitive. A different subject = que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Pleasure at something is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me alegra que pases el verano aquí.
examples.en: I'm glad you're spending the summer here.
examples.note: Pasar el verano = spend the summer.

examples.es: Me alegra que gasten menos energía.
examples.en: I'm glad they use less energy.
examples.note: Gastar energía = to use up energy.

examples.es: Me alegra que ya no gastes tanto en ropa.
examples.en: I'm glad you don't spend so much on clothes any more.
examples.note: Gastar en = to spend on.

contrast.es: Veo que ya no gastas tanto en ropa.
contrast.en: I see you don't spend so much on clothes any more.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Mientras + subjunctive means 'as long as', for something that's ongoing or hasn't happened.

examples.es: Mientras gastes con cuidado, no hay problema.
examples.en: As long as you spend carefully, there's no problem.
examples.note: Mientras + subjunctive = as long as.

examples.es: Mientras pasemos tiempo juntos, soy feliz.
examples.en: As long as we spend time together, I'm happy.
examples.note: Pasar tiempo = to spend time.

examples.es: Mientras pases tiempo con ellos, serás feliz.
examples.en: As long as you spend time with them, you'll be happy.
examples.note: A condition about the future, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Mientras pasas tiempo con ellos, eres feliz.
contrast.en: While you spend time with them, you're happy.
contrast.note: Mientras + indicative = an actual, simultaneous situation. Mientras + subjunctive = as long as.

tricky: Gastar and pasar are both regular (gaste, pase), and neither has a stem change. The catch is which one you use: money is gastar, time you enjoy is pasar ('que pases el verano'), and time wasted is perder.

title: hablar vs decir

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quiero que hables con él.
examples.en: I want you to talk to him.
examples.note: Hablar con = to talk with. Regular.

examples.es: Quiero que me digas la verdad.
examples.en: I want you to tell me the truth.
examples.note: Decir is irregular: digas, not 'dices'.

examples.es: Quiero que me digas que me quieres.
examples.en: I want you to tell me that you love me.
examples.note: Decir que = to say that. The first que triggers the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Me dices que me quieres.
contrast.en: You tell me you love me.
contrast.note: Reporting what's said uses the indicative. Wanting someone to say it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Liking something is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me gusta que hables despacio.
examples.en: I like it that you speak slowly.
examples.note: Me gusta que + subjunctive when someone else is the subject.

examples.es: Me gusta que me digas lo que piensas.
examples.en: I like that you tell me what you think.
examples.note: Decir lo que = to say what. Digas is irregular.

examples.es: Me gusta que ella hable tantos idiomas.
examples.en: I like that she speaks so many languages.
examples.note: Hablar + language = to speak a language.

contrast.es: Sé que ella habla tantos idiomas.
contrast.en: I know she speaks so many languages.
contrast.note: Sé que takes the indicative. Me gusta que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hasn't happened yet.

examples.es: Cuéntamelo antes de que hable con ella.
examples.en: Tell me before he talks to her.
examples.note: Antes de que + different subjects always means subjunctive.

examples.es: Díselo antes de que lo diga otra persona.
examples.en: Tell her before someone else does.
examples.note: Decir: diga, irregular.

examples.es: Habla con ella antes de que hable con tu jefe.
examples.en: Talk to her before she talks to your boss.
examples.note: The talking hasn't happened yet.

contrast.es: Hablé con ella después de que habló con tu jefe.
contrast.en: I talked to her after she talked to your boss.
contrast.note: Después de que + a completed event takes the indicative.

tricky: Decir is irregular: diga, digas, digamos, digan, never 'dica' or 'dize'. Hablar is regular: hable. The mood changes the meaning: 'te digo que vengas' is an order (subjunctive) but 'te digo que vienes' reports a fact (indicative).

title: encontrar vs buscar

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá encuentres lo que buscas.
examples.en: I hope you find what you're looking for.
examples.note: O→ue stem: encuentres. 'Buscas' stays indicative because it's a fact.

examples.es: Ojalá encontremos un hotel barato.
examples.en: I hope we find a cheap hotel.
examples.note: Nosotros keeps the o: encontremos, never 'encuentremos'.

examples.es: Ojalá encuentren a mi perro.
examples.en: I hope they find my dog.
examples.note: A hope about something not yet achieved.

contrast.es: Encontraron a mi perro.
contrast.en: They found my dog.
contrast.note: Ojalá + subjunctive = a hope. Indicative = a fact.

triggers.explanation: Judging how hard something is, is an evaluation, not a statement of fact.

examples.es: Es difícil que encuentres un buen taxi aquí.
examples.en: It's hard for you to find a good taxi here.
examples.note: Es difícil que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Es difícil que busquen otra solución.
examples.en: It's unlikely they'll look for another solution.
examples.note: Buscar: c→qu before e, busquen.

examples.es: Es difícil que encuentre trabajo sin experiencia.
examples.en: It's hard for him to find a job without experience.
examples.note: Evaluating how difficult something is, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Es verdad que encuentra trabajo sin experiencia.
contrast.en: It's true that he finds jobs without experience.
contrast.note: Es verdad states a fact (indicative). Es difícil que gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Tan pronto como about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Tan pronto como encuentre las llaves, salimos.
examples.en: As soon as I find the keys, we'll leave.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Tan pronto como busque en el sótano, te aviso.
examples.en: As soon as I look in the basement, I'll let you know.
examples.note: Buscar en = to look in.

examples.es: Tan pronto como encuentres trabajo, te mudarás.
examples.en: As soon as you find a job, you'll move.
examples.note: Future, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Tan pronto como encontró trabajo, se mudó.
contrast.en: As soon as he found a job, he moved.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Encontrar changes o→ue (encuentre, encuentres, encuentren) except nosotros (encontremos). Buscar changes c→qu before e: busque, busques, busquemos, never 'busce'. 'Que busques' is the effort, and 'que encuentres' is the result.

title: perder vs faltar

triggers.explanation: Not wanting something to happen is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No quiero que pierdas el tren.
examples.en: I don't want you to miss the train.
examples.note: Perder el tren = to miss the train. E→ie stem: pierdas.

examples.es: No quiero que falte nada en la fiesta.
examples.en: I don't want anything to be missing at the party.
examples.note: Faltar = to be missing / lacking. The subject is the thing that's missing: nada.

examples.es: No quiero que pierdas la esperanza.
examples.en: I don't want you to lose hope.
examples.note: Perder la esperanza = to lose hope.

contrast.es: Veo que pierdes la esperanza.
contrast.en: I see you're losing hope.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. A wish uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Regret is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es una pena que pierdas tanto tiempo.
examples.en: It's a shame you waste so much time.
examples.note: Perder tiempo = to waste time.

examples.es: Es una pena que falten tantos jugadores.
examples.en: It's a shame so many players are missing.
examples.note: Plural subject, so falten.

examples.es: Es una pena que Luis falte a la boda.
examples.en: It's a shame Luis is missing the wedding.
examples.note: Faltar a = to miss (not attend) an event.

contrast.es: Es cierto que Luis falta a la boda.
contrast.en: It's true that Luis is missing the wedding.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es una pena reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: A no ser que means 'unless', and it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Llegaremos a tiempo, a no ser que perdamos el tren.
examples.en: We'll arrive on time, unless we miss the train.
examples.note: Nosotros keeps the e: perdamos, never 'pierdamos'.

examples.es: Empezamos ya, a no ser que falte algo.
examples.en: We'll start now, unless something is missing.
examples.note: Faltar here = to be missing.

examples.es: Llegará mañana, a no ser que se pierda el paquete.
examples.en: It'll arrive tomorrow, unless the parcel gets lost.
examples.note: Se pierde = it gets lost. The reflexive makes it happen to the object.

contrast.es: Llegará mañana si no se pierde el paquete.
contrast.en: It'll arrive tomorrow if the parcel doesn't get lost.
contrast.note: Si + present indicative expresses a similar condition. A no ser que always needs the subjunctive.

tricky: Perder has an e→ie stem change (pierda, pierdas, pierdan) but perdamos for nosotros. Faltar works like gustar: 'me falte' (I lack), not 'falto'. Faltar a means to miss (skip) an event: 'que no faltes a clase'. And 'se pierda' (it gets lost) is different from 'pierda' (loses it).

title: tocar vs jugar

triggers.explanation: Suggesting something is an attempt to influence, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Propongo que juguemos a las cartas.
examples.en: I suggest we play cards.
examples.note: Jugar a + game. Nosotros: juguemos has gu but no stem change.

examples.es: Propongo que Pablo juegue de portero.
examples.en: I suggest Pablo plays in goal.
examples.note: Jugar changes u→ue and adds gu: juegue.

examples.es: Propongo que toquemos esta canción en la fiesta.
examples.en: I suggest we play this song at the party.
examples.note: Tocar needs c→qu before e: toquemos.

contrast.es: Tocamos esta canción en la fiesta.
contrast.en: We play this song at the party.
contrast.note: A plain statement uses the indicative. A suggestion uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que juegue hoy.
examples.en: I don't think he'll play today.
examples.note: Jugar = to play a game or sport.

examples.es: No creo que toque bien la guitarra.
examples.en: I don't think he plays the guitar well.
examples.note: Tocar + instrument. C→qu: toque.

examples.es: No creo que Pablo juegue al tenis.
examples.en: I don't think Pablo plays tennis.
examples.note: Jugar al + sport.

contrast.es: Creo que Pablo juega al tenis.
contrast.en: I think Pablo plays tennis.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event that hasn't happened yet takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando juegues con tu hermano, ten cuidado.
examples.en: When you play with your brother, be careful.
examples.note: A future occasion, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando toque en el concierto, estaremos en primera fila.
examples.en: When he plays at the concert, we'll be in the front row.
examples.note: C→qu: toque. Future event.

examples.es: Cuando juguemos la final, estarás aquí.
examples.en: When we play the final, you'll be here.
examples.note: A future match, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando jugamos los domingos, estás aquí.
contrast.en: Whenever we play on Sundays, you're here.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Jugar is the only Spanish verb with a u→ue stem change, and it also needs gu: juegue, juegues, jueguen, but juguemos in nosotros. Tocar needs c→qu: toque, toques, toquemos, never 'toce'. Jugar goes with a (jugar al fútbol) and tocar goes with instruments (tocar la guitarra).

title: volver vs regresar

triggers.explanation: Worry is an emotional reaction to something uncertain, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me preocupa que no regrese a tiempo.
examples.en: I'm worried he won't be back on time.
examples.note: Regresar is regular: regrese.

examples.es: Me preocupa que no vuelvas pronto.
examples.en: I'm worried you won't come back soon.
examples.note: Volver has o→ue: vuelvas.

examples.es: Me preocupa que nunca vuelva a casa.
examples.en: I'm worried she'll never come home.
examples.note: Volver a casa = to come back home.

contrast.es: Sé que nunca vuelve a casa.
contrast.en: I know she never comes home.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Me preocupa que expresses worry (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Quizás expresses doubt, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quizás regrese mañana.
examples.en: Maybe he'll be back tomorrow.
examples.note: Quizás + subjunctive = genuine doubt.

examples.es: Quizás vuelvan en verano.
examples.en: Maybe they'll come back in the summer.
examples.note: Ellos form: vuelvan.

examples.es: Quizás no vuelva a llamar nunca.
examples.en: Maybe he'll never call again.
examples.note: Volver a + infinitive = to do again.

contrast.es: Seguro que no vuelve a llamar nunca.
contrast.en: I'm sure he'll never call again.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Quizás = doubt (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Siempre que + subjunctive means 'as long as' or 'whenever' in the future.

examples.es: Siempre que regreses, tendrás casa aquí.
examples.en: Whenever you come back, you'll have a home here.
examples.note: Future 'whenever': subjunctive.

examples.es: Siempre que regresemos a tiempo, iremos al cine.
examples.en: As long as we get back in time, we'll go to the cinema.
examples.note: Siempre que = provided that.

examples.es: Siempre que vuelvas tarde, avísame.
examples.en: Whenever you come back late, let me know.
examples.note: Future-oriented request.

contrast.es: Siempre que vuelves tarde, me avisas.
contrast.en: Whenever you come back late, you let me know.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future instruction uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Volver has an o→ue stem change (vuelva, vuelvas, vuelvan) but volvamos in nosotros. Regresar is regular: regrese. In Spain regresar can sound more formal, while in Latin America it's everyday. Volver a + infinitive means 'do again': 'que vuelvas a intentarlo'.

title: dejar vs salir (leave)

triggers.explanation: Refusing to allow something is an attempt to influence, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No permito que dejes la puerta abierta.
examples.en: I won't allow you to leave the door open.
examples.note: Dejar = to leave something behind. Regular: dejes.

examples.es: No permito que salgas sin abrigo.
examples.en: I won't let you go out without a coat.
examples.note: Salir is irregular: salgas, with -g-.

examples.es: No permito que lo dejes todo por un capricho.
examples.en: I won't let you give everything up on a whim.
examples.note: Dejarlo todo = to give everything up.

contrast.es: Veo que lo dejas todo por un capricho.
contrast.en: I see you're giving everything up on a whim.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Forbidding it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Calling something logical is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es lógico que salgas temprano.
examples.en: It's logical that you leave early.
examples.note: Salir = to leave a place.

examples.es: Es lógico que deje el trabajo si no le pagan.
examples.en: It's logical that she leaves the job if they don't pay her.
examples.note: Dejar el trabajo = to quit the job.

examples.es: Es lógico que salga de casa a los treinta.
examples.en: It's logical that he leaves home at thirty.
examples.note: Salir de casa = to move out.

contrast.es: Es cierto que sale de casa a los treinta.
contrast.en: It's true that he leaves home at thirty.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es lógico judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Salvo que means 'unless', and it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me quedo en casa, salvo que salga el sol.
examples.en: I'll stay home, unless the sun comes out.
examples.note: Salir = to come out (of the sun).

examples.es: Salvo que deje de llover, nos quedamos en casa.
examples.en: Unless it stops raining, we're staying at home.
examples.note: Dejar de + infinitive = to stop. Deje de llover = it stops raining.

examples.es: Salvo que salgas antes, llegarás tarde.
examples.en: Unless you leave earlier, you'll be late.
examples.note: Future condition, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Si no sales antes, llegarás tarde.
contrast.en: If you don't leave earlier, you'll be late.
contrast.note: Si + present indicative expresses a similar condition. Salvo que always needs the subjunctive.

tricky: Dejar and salir both translate 'leave', but dejar is to leave something or someone behind (deje) and salir is to go out of a place (salga, irregular with -g-). Dejar de + infinitive means to stop ('que dejes de fumar'), and dejar + infinitive means to let ('que me dejes entrar').

title: ser vs parecer

triggers.explanation: Denying that something seems to be so, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No me parece que sea buena idea.
examples.en: I don't think it's a good idea.
examples.note: No me parece que + subjunctive.

examples.es: No me parece que sea tan caro como dices.
examples.en: I don't think it's as expensive as you say.
examples.note: Parecer states an impression, ser the fact itself.

examples.es: No me parece que sea de fiar.
examples.en: I don't think he's trustworthy.
examples.note: Ser de fiar = to be trustworthy.

contrast.es: Me parece que es de fiar.
contrast.en: It seems to me he's trustworthy.
contrast.note: Me parece que takes the indicative. No me parece que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something uncertain or hypothetical.

examples.es: Aunque parezca fácil, no lo es.
examples.en: Even if it seems easy, it isn't.
examples.note: Parecer + adjective = to seem. Parezca has -zc-.

examples.es: Aunque parezca mentira, es verdad.
examples.en: Believe it or not, it's true.
examples.note: Aunque parezca mentira is a fixed expression: literally 'even if it seems a lie'.

examples.es: Aunque parezca cansado, sigue trabajando.
examples.en: Even if he seems tired, he keeps working.
examples.note: You aren't sure he seems tired, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Aunque parece cansado, sigue trabajando.
contrast.en: Although he seems tired, he keeps working.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

triggers.explanation: Por muy + adjective + que means 'however', and it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Por muy simple que parezca, funciona.
examples.en: However simple it seems, it works.
examples.note: Por muy... que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Por muy caro que sea, lo compraré.
examples.en: However expensive it is, I'll buy it.
examples.note: Concession: whatever the price may be.

examples.es: Por muy tranquilo que parezca, está nervioso.
examples.en: However calm he seems, he is nervous.
examples.note: Parecer = the appearance; estar = the real state.

contrast.es: Parece tranquilo, pero está nervioso.
contrast.en: He seems calm, but he's nervous.
contrast.note: A flat statement uses the indicative. Por muy... que concedes a point (subjunctive).

tricky: Parecer takes -zc- in the subjunctive: parezca, parezcas, parezcamos, never 'parece' or 'parezga'. 'Parece que' takes the indicative but 'no parece que' takes the subjunctive. 'Aunque parezca mentira' is a fixed phrase, and 'se parece a' means looks like, a different verb.

title: haber

triggers.explanation: A possibility isn't a fact, so the subjunctive is needed.

examples.es: Es posible que haya clase mañana.
examples.en: It's possible there will be a class tomorrow.
examples.note: Hay becomes haya in the subjunctive. Never 'haiga'.

examples.es: Es posible que ya hayan llegado.
examples.en: It's possible they've already arrived.
examples.note: Haber as an auxiliary agrees with the subject: hayan, plus the participle.

examples.es: Es posible que haya veinte libros en la caja.
examples.en: It's possible there are twenty books in the box.
examples.note: Impersonal haya stays singular even with a plural noun: 'haya veinte libros', not 'hayan'.

contrast.es: Hay veinte libros en la caja.
contrast.en: There are twenty books in the box.
contrast.note: Indicative hay never changes for plurals, and neither does haya in the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá haya sol mañana.
examples.en: I hope there's sun tomorrow.
examples.note: Ojalá + haya = I hope there is.

examples.es: Ojalá hayas dormido bien.
examples.en: I hope you've slept well.
examples.note: The present perfect subjunctive: haber in the subjunctive + the participle.

examples.es: Ojalá hayan llegado ya a casa.
examples.en: I hope they've got home already.
examples.note: A hope about something that may already have happened.

contrast.es: Han llegado ya a casa.
contrast.en: They have got home already.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative han. A hope uses hayan.

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto haya noticias, te aviso.
examples.en: As soon as there's news, I'll let you know.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto hayas comido, salimos.
examples.en: As soon as you've eaten, we'll go out.
examples.note: En cuanto + present perfect subjunctive = once something is complete.

examples.es: En cuanto haya sitio, nos sentamos.
examples.en: As soon as there's room, we'll sit down.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: En cuanto hay sitio, nos sentamos.
contrast.en: As soon as there's room, we sit down.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Hay becomes haya in the subjunctive, never 'haiga', and it stays singular for plural nouns: 'es posible que haya veinte libros', not 'hayan'. As an auxiliary it agrees: 'hayan llegado'. Don't confuse it with 'halla' (hallar) or the noun la haya (beech tree).

title: tener

triggers.explanation: Reacting to something as lucky is an emotional evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es una suerte que tengas tiempo.
examples.en: It's lucky that you have time.
examples.note: Tener has -g- in the subjunctive: tengas.

examples.es: Es una suerte que tengamos tan buenos vecinos.
examples.en: It's lucky that we have such good neighbours.
examples.note: Nosotros: tengamos.

examples.es: Es una suerte que no tengan hambre.
examples.en: It's lucky that they aren't hungry.
examples.note: Tener hambre = to be hungry. The expression keeps tener.

contrast.es: Es cierto que no tienen hambre.
contrast.en: It's true that they aren't hungry.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es una suerte reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando tengas hambre, come algo.
examples.en: When you're hungry, eat something.
examples.note: Tener hambre = to be hungry.

examples.es: Cuando tengamos prisa, tomaremos un taxi.
examples.en: When we're in a hurry, we'll take a taxi.
examples.note: Tener prisa = to be in a hurry.

examples.es: Cuando tengas frío, avísame.
examples.en: When you're cold, let me know.
examples.note: A future possibility, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando tienes frío, te pones la chaqueta.
contrast.en: When you're cold, you put on a jacket.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: When the person you describe isn't identified, the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Necesito a alguien que tenga paciencia.
examples.en: I need someone who has patience.
examples.note: Alguien = unidentified, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Necesito a alguien que tenga ganas de trabajar.
examples.en: I need someone who feels like working.
examples.note: Tener ganas de = to feel like.

examples.es: Necesito a alguien que tenga coche.
examples.en: I need someone who has a car.
examples.note: Any such person, existence unknown.

contrast.es: Conozco a alguien que tiene coche.
contrast.en: I know someone who has a car.
contrast.note: A specific person who exists takes the indicative.

tricky: Tener keeps its -g- in the subjunctive: tenga, tengas, tengamos, tengan, never 'tienga' or 'teniga'. The fixed tener expressions stay with tener: 'que tengas hambre / razón / prisa', not 'estés'. Tener que + infinitive keeps tener: 'no creo que tengas que ir'.

title: hacer

triggers.explanation: A possibility isn't a fact, so the subjunctive is needed.

examples.es: Es posible que haga calor mañana.
examples.en: It's possible it'll be hot tomorrow.
examples.note: Weather uses hacer in the third person singular: haga.

examples.es: Es posible que no hagamos nada este fin de semana.
examples.en: It's possible we won't do anything this weekend.
examples.note: Hacer is irregular: hagamos.

examples.es: Es posible que haga frío esta noche.
examples.en: It's possible it'll be cold tonight.
examples.note: Weather: hacer frío / calor / viento.

contrast.es: Seguro que hace frío esta noche.
contrast.en: It's certain it'll be cold tonight.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Es posible que = possibility (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Insisting on something is pressing someone to act, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Insisto en que hagas la tarea.
examples.en: I insist that you do the homework.
examples.note: Insistir en que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Insisto en que me hagas caso.
examples.en: I insist that you listen to me.
examples.note: Hacer caso = to pay attention to / obey.

examples.es: Insisto en que lo hagas tú mismo.
examples.en: I insist that you do it yourself.
examples.note: A different subject than the speaker.

contrast.es: Insisto en hacerlo yo mismo.
contrast.en: I insist on doing it myself.
contrast.note: Same subject = infinitive. A different subject = que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: En caso de que introduces a possibility, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Lleva abrigo en caso de que haga frío.
examples.en: Take a coat in case it's cold.
examples.note: En caso de que always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Compra más en caso de que hagamos una fiesta.
examples.en: Buy more in case we have a party.
examples.note: Hacer una fiesta = to have/throw a party.

examples.es: En caso de que haga mal tiempo, cancelamos.
examples.en: In case it's bad weather, we cancel.
examples.note: Weather expression.

contrast.es: Si hace mal tiempo, cancelamos.
contrast.en: If it's bad weather, we cancel.
contrast.note: Si + present indicative says something similar. En caso de que always needs the subjunctive.

tricky: Hacer is irregular: haga, hagas, hagamos, hagan, never 'haca' or 'hace'. Weather and time hace stay singular: 'es posible que haga frío', 'no creo que haga dos años que vivo aquí'. Only the first verb changes.

title: dar

triggers.explanation: Saying what is advisable is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Conviene que des las gracias.
examples.en: It's advisable that you say thank you.
examples.note: Dar las gracias = to say thank you.

examples.es: Conviene que me des tu número.
examples.en: It's a good idea for you to give me your number.
examples.note: Dar is irregular: des.

examples.es: Conviene que le dé tiempo a decidir.
examples.en: It's advisable that you give him time to decide.
examples.note: Dé needs an accent to tell it from the preposition de.

contrast.es: Es evidente que le da tiempo a decidir.
contrast.en: It's obvious that he gives him time to decide.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Conviene que advises (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Indifference toward something is a reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me da igual que me den el puesto.
examples.en: I don't care if they give me the job.
examples.note: Dar igual = to not matter.

examples.es: Me da igual que te dé la razón.
examples.en: I don't care if he agrees with you.
examples.note: Dar la razón a alguien = to agree with someone.

examples.es: Me da igual que nos den una respuesta mañana.
examples.en: I don't mind if they give us an answer tomorrow.
examples.note: A reaction to a possible event.

contrast.es: Sé que nos dan una respuesta mañana.
contrast.en: I know they're giving us an answer tomorrow.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Me da igual que reacts (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando me des tu número, te llamo.
examples.en: When you give me your number, I'll call you.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando le dé el regalo, se pondrá contento.
examples.en: When I give him the present, he'll be happy.
examples.note: Dé has an accent here: first or third person singular.

examples.es: Cuando se dé cuenta, será tarde.
examples.en: By the time he realises, it'll be too late.
examples.note: Darse cuenta de = to realise.

contrast.es: Cuando se da cuenta, se enfada.
contrast.en: When he realises, he gets angry.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Dar's present subjunctive is dé (with an accent), des, dé, demos, den. Only dé carries the accent, to separate it from the preposition de: 'quiero que me dé' vs 'una taza de té'. The dar expressions keep dar: 'me da pena que', 'me da igual que'.

title: poner

triggers.explanation: Saying something isn't necessary is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No es necesario que pongas la mesa.
examples.en: You don't need to set the table.
examples.note: Poner la mesa = to set the table. Poner has a -g-.

examples.es: No es necesario que te pongas el abrigo.
examples.en: You don't need to put your coat on.
examples.note: Ponerse + clothing = to put on.

examples.es: No es necesario que se ponga nervioso.
examples.en: There's no need for him to get nervous.
examples.note: Ponerse + adjective = to become (temporary emotional change).

contrast.es: Se pone nervioso en los exámenes.
contrast.en: He gets nervous in exams.
contrast.note: A plain fact uses the indicative. A judgement uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Annoyance is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me da rabia que pongan la música tan alta.
examples.en: It infuriates me that they play the music so loud.
examples.note: Poner la música = to put on music.

examples.es: Me da rabia que me pongan tantas pegas.
examples.en: It infuriates me that they raise so many objections.
examples.note: Poner pegas = to raise objections (Spain).

examples.es: Me da rabia que se ponga a gritar por todo.
examples.en: It infuriates me that he starts shouting at everything.
examples.note: Ponerse a + infinitive = to start doing.

contrast.es: Se pone a gritar por todo.
contrast.en: He starts shouting at everything.
contrast.note: A plain fact uses the indicative. A reaction uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando pongas la mesa, avísame.
examples.en: When you've set the table, let me know.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando se ponga el sol, volvemos.
examples.en: When the sun sets, we'll go back.
examples.note: Ponerse el sol = the sun sets.

examples.es: Cuando te pongas nervioso, respira hondo.
examples.en: When you get nervous, take a deep breath.
examples.note: A future possibility, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando te pones nervioso, respiras hondo.
contrast.en: When you get nervous, you breathe deeply.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.
