tricky: Poner has a -g-: ponga, pongas, pongamos, pongan, like tener and venir. Don't drop the -se for 'become': 'que se ponga nervioso', not 'que ponga nervioso'. Ponerse + clothes = put on, and ponerse a + infinitive = start to.

title: gustar

triggers.explanation: When what you describe isn't identified yet, the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Busco algo que le guste a mi madre.
examples.en: I'm looking for something my mother will like.
examples.note: The thing isn't chosen yet, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Busco algo que les guste a mis hijos.
examples.en: I'm looking for something my children will like.
examples.note: Gustar agrees with algo (singular), not with los hijos: guste, never 'gusten'.

examples.es: Busco algo que guste a todos.
examples.en: I'm looking for something everyone will like.
examples.note: Unknown thing, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Conozco algo que gusta a todos.
contrast.en: I know something that everyone likes.
contrast.note: Something that exists and you know takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Hoping for something involves a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Espero que te guste la sorpresa.
examples.en: I hope you like the surprise.
examples.note: Gustar agrees with la sorpresa: singular, so guste.

examples.es: Espero que les gusten las flores.
examples.en: I hope they like the flowers.
examples.note: Las flores is plural, so gusten.

examples.es: Espero que te guste mi nuevo corte de pelo.
examples.en: I hope you like my new haircut.
examples.note: A hope about someone's reaction.

contrast.es: Sé que te gusta mi nuevo corte de pelo.
contrast.en: I know you like my new haircut.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Espero que expresses a hope (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something not established as true.

examples.es: Aunque no me guste, lo como.
examples.en: Even if I don't like it, I'll eat it.
examples.note: A hypothetical dislike, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Aunque no le gusten los deportes, viene con nosotros.
examples.en: Even if he doesn't like sports, he comes with us.
examples.note: Los deportes is plural, so gusten.

examples.es: Aunque no te guste el café, pruébalo.
examples.en: Even if you don't like coffee, try it.
examples.note: You don't know whether you'll like it.

contrast.es: Aunque no te gusta el café, lo bebes.
contrast.en: Although you don't like coffee, you drink it.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Gustar agrees with the thing liked, not the person: 'que te guste el libro' but 'que te gusten los libros'. The subjunctive is guste/gusten, never 'gusto' (which would mean 'I please'). And 'me gusta que' takes the subjunctive, but 'me gusta correr' just needs an infinitive.

title: tomar

triggers.explanation: Recommending something is trying to influence, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te recomiendo que tomes un taxi.
examples.en: I recommend that you take a taxi.
examples.note: Regular verb: tomes.

examples.es: Te recomiendo que tomes una decisión pronto.
examples.en: I recommend that you make a decision soon.
examples.note: Tomar una decisión = to make a decision. Never 'hacer una decisión'.

examples.es: Te recomiendo que tomes esta medicina antes de comer.
examples.en: I recommend that you take this medicine before eating.
examples.note: Tomar = to take medicine.

contrast.es: Sé que tomas esta medicina antes de comer.
contrast.en: I know you take this medicine before eating.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Recomendar expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te doy dinero para que tomes un taxi.
examples.en: I'm giving you money so you can take a taxi.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Te llamo para que tomemos un café.
examples.en: I'm calling you so that we can have a coffee.
examples.note: Tomar un café = to have a coffee.

examples.es: Les doy una semana para que tomen una decisión.
examples.en: I'm giving them a week so that they can make a decision.
examples.note: Different subjects (I / they), so para que + subjunctive.

contrast.es: Quedamos para tomar una decisión juntos.
contrast.en: We're meeting to make a decision together.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que tome café.
examples.en: I don't think he drinks coffee.
examples.note: Tomar café = to drink coffee.

examples.es: No creo que tomen la decisión hoy.
examples.en: I don't think they'll make the decision today.
examples.note: Ellos form: tomen.

examples.es: No creo que tome el autobús para ir al trabajo.
examples.en: I don't think she takes the bus to get to work.
examples.note: Tomar el autobús = to take the bus. In Spain you'll also hear coger el autobús; in much of Latin America use tomar.

contrast.es: Creo que toma el autobús para ir al trabajo.
contrast.en: I think she takes the bus to get to work.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Tomar is regular (tome, tomes, tomemos, tomen), so the catches are in the meaning. It covers drink, eat, take transport and decisions: 'que tomes una decisión', never 'hagas una decisión'. In Spain you can also say coger el autobús, but in much of Latin America coger is vulgar, so tomar is the safe choice.

title: coger

triggers.explanation: Suggesting something is trying to influence, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Sugiero que cojas el tren.
examples.en: I suggest that you take the train.
examples.note: G→j before e: cojas, never 'cogas'. In Spain coger el tren is normal.

examples.es: Sugiero que cojamos un atajo.
examples.en: I suggest we take a shortcut.
examples.note: Coger un atajo = to take a shortcut (Spain). In Latin America tomar un atajo.

examples.es: Sugiero que cojas un taxi.
examples.en: I suggest you take a taxi.
examples.note: In much of Latin America coger is vulgar, so use tomar un taxi there.

contrast.es: Sé que coges un taxi cada día.
contrast.en: I know you take a taxi every day.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Sugerir expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Después de que about an event that hasn't happened yet takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Después de que cojas las llaves, cierra la puerta.
examples.en: After you pick up the keys, close the door.
examples.note: Coger = to pick up, to take.

examples.es: Después de que coja el autobús, te llamo.
examples.en: After I take the bus, I'll call you.
examples.note: G→j: coja.

examples.es: Después de que coja las vacaciones, empiezo a estudiar.
examples.en: After I take my holiday, I'll start studying.
examples.note: Coger vacaciones = to take time off (Spain).

contrast.es: Después de que cogí las vacaciones, empecé a estudiar.
contrast.en: After I took my holiday, I started studying.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: A possibility isn't a fact, so the subjunctive is needed.

examples.es: Es posible que coja el autobús.
examples.en: It's possible I'll take the bus.
examples.note: Coger el autobús is normal in Spain.

examples.es: Es posible que cojamos el último tren.
examples.en: It's possible we'll catch the last train.
examples.note: Coger un tren = to catch a train.

examples.es: Es posible que cojas frío sin abrigo.
examples.en: It's possible you'll catch a chill without a coat.
examples.note: Coger frío = to catch a chill (Spain). In Latin America: resfriarse, agarrar frío.

contrast.es: Seguro que coges frío sin abrigo.
contrast.en: You'll definitely catch a chill without a coat.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Es posible que = possibility (subjunctive).

tricky: Coger needs g→j before e: coja, cojas, cojamos, cojan, never 'coga'. The real catch is regional: in Spain coger is everyday and innocent (take, catch, grab), but in much of Latin America (Mexico, Argentina and elsewhere) it's vulgar, so use tomar, agarrar or llevar there.

title: entrar

triggers.explanation: Forbidding someone is influencing them, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Prohíbo que entres en mi cuarto.
examples.en: I forbid you to go into my room.
examples.note: Entrar en = to enter. In Latin America you'll also hear entrar a.

examples.es: Prohíbo que entren sin llamar.
examples.en: I forbid them to come in without knocking.
examples.note: Ellos form: entren.

examples.es: Prohíbo que entres en mi cuarto sin permiso.
examples.en: I forbid you to enter my room without permission.
examples.note: A different subject, so que + subjunctive.

contrast.es: Sé que entras en mi cuarto sin permiso.
contrast.en: I know you go into my room without permission.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Prohibir expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Abro la puerta para que entre el aire.
examples.en: I'm opening the door so the air can come in.
examples.note: Entre has el aire as the subject.

examples.es: Dejo la llave para que entres en casa.
examples.en: I'm leaving the key so you can get into the house.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Espérame para que entremos juntos.
examples.en: Wait for me so that we go in together.
examples.note: Nosotros includes the speaker.

contrast.es: Espérame para entrar juntos.
contrast.en: Wait for me to go in together.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Surprise is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me extraña que no entren.
examples.en: It surprises me that they aren't coming in.
examples.note: Extrañar here = to surprise.

examples.es: Me extraña que entres sin llamar.
examples.en: It surprises me that you walk in without knocking.
examples.note: Entrar sin llamar = to go in without knocking.

examples.es: Me extraña que entren en la reunión sin invitación.
examples.en: It surprises me that they come into the meeting without an invitation.
examples.note: A reaction to a fact.

contrast.es: Sé que entran en la reunión sin invitación.
contrast.en: I know they come into the meeting without an invitation.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Me extraña que reacts (subjunctive).

tricky: Entrar is regular: entre, entres, entremos, entren. The catch is the preposition: entrar en is standard in Spain, and entrar a is common in Latin America. Never 'entrar la casa' without one. 'Que entre' is also a polite command: 'que entre el siguiente'.

title: subir vs bajar

triggers.explanation: Saying something isn't needed is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No hace falta que subas la maleta.
examples.en: You don't need to carry the suitcase up.
examples.note: Subir + object = to carry up.

examples.es: No hace falta que bajemos todavía.
examples.en: We don't need to go down yet.
examples.note: Bajar = to go down.

examples.es: No hace falta que bajes la música.
examples.en: You don't need to turn the music down.
examples.note: Bajar la música = to turn the music down.

contrast.es: Siempre bajas la música a las diez.
contrast.en: You always turn the music down at ten.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. Denying a need uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Likelihood isn't certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es probable que suban los precios.
examples.en: It's likely that prices will go up.
examples.note: Subir = to rise.

examples.es: Es probable que baje la temperatura.
examples.en: It's likely that the temperature will drop.
examples.note: Bajar = to fall, drop.

examples.es: Es probable que suban el sueldo en enero.
examples.en: It's likely they'll raise the salary in January.
examples.note: Subir el sueldo = to raise the salary.

contrast.es: Seguro que suben el sueldo en enero.
contrast.en: I'm sure they'll raise the salary in January.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Es probable que = likelihood (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Hasta que about something not yet completed takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Espera hasta que suba el ascensor.
examples.en: Wait until the lift comes up.
examples.note: The lift hasn't arrived yet.

examples.es: No salgas hasta que baje la fiebre.
examples.en: Don't go out until your fever goes down.
examples.note: Bajar la fiebre = for a fever to drop.

examples.es: Espera en el coche hasta que suba tu hermano.
examples.en: Wait in the car until your brother gets in.
examples.note: Subir al coche = to get into the car.

contrast.es: Esperé en el coche hasta que subió tu hermano.
contrast.en: I waited in the car until your brother got in.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Subir and bajar are regular (suba, baje, bajemos). The catches are the prepositions: subir a / bajar de for vehicles ('que subas al tren', 'que bajes del tren'), and for carrying things they take a direct object: 'que subas las maletas'.

title: tirar vs sacar

triggers.explanation: Asking someone formally is a request, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te ruego que tires la basura.
examples.en: Please throw out the rubbish.
examples.note: Tirar la basura = to put rubbish in the bin.

examples.es: Te ruego que saques al perro.
examples.en: Please take the dog out.
examples.note: Sacar needs c→qu: saques, never 'sacas' or 'saces'.

examples.es: Te ruego que no tires esos papeles.
examples.en: Please don't throw those papers away.
examples.note: Tirar = to throw away.

contrast.es: Sé que tiras esos papeles.
contrast.en: I know you throw those papers away.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Rogar expresses a request (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Saying it's time for something is a judgement about what should happen, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es hora de que tires esos zapatos.
examples.en: It's time you threw those shoes out.
examples.note: Tirar = to throw away.

examples.es: Es hora de que saques el carné de conducir.
examples.en: It's time you got your driving licence.
examples.note: Sacar el carné = to get a licence.

examples.es: Es hora de que saquemos conclusiones.
examples.en: It's time we drew conclusions.
examples.note: Sacar conclusiones = to draw conclusions.

contrast.es: Es hora de sacar conclusiones.
contrast.en: It's time to draw conclusions.
contrast.note: A general statement uses the infinitive. Naming who acts uses que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Una vez que about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Una vez que tires la basura, ven.
examples.en: Once you've thrown out the rubbish, come over.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Una vez que saques el billete, espera aquí.
examples.en: Once you've got your ticket, wait here.
examples.note: Sacar el billete = to get a ticket (Spain). In Latin America: boleto.

examples.es: Una vez que saquemos las entradas, te aviso.
examples.en: Once we've got the tickets, I'll let you know.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Una vez que sacamos las entradas, no hay devolución.
contrast.en: Once we've bought the tickets, there's no refund.
contrast.note: A general fact uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Sacar needs c→qu: saque, saques, saquemos, never 'sace'. Tirar is regular (tire), but its meanings multiply: throw, pull, throw away, waste. And remember tirar la basura = put it in the bin, while sacar la basura = take the bag out to the street.

title: echar

triggers.explanation: Calling something natural is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es natural que eches de menos a tu familia.
examples.en: It's natural that you miss your family.
examples.note: Echar de menos = to miss. In Latin America extrañar is more common.

examples.es: Es natural que se echen a reír.
examples.en: It's natural that they burst out laughing.
examples.note: Echarse a + infinitive = to burst out.

examples.es: Es natural que te eche de menos.
examples.en: It's natural that he misses you.
examples.note: Echar de menos = to miss someone.

contrast.es: Es cierto que te echa de menos.
contrast.en: It's true that he misses you.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es natural judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ponlo en la nevera para que no se eche a perder.
examples.en: Put it in the fridge so it doesn't go off.
examples.note: Echarse a perder = to go bad.

examples.es: Dame el informe para que le eche un vistazo.
examples.en: Give me the report so I can have a look at it.
examples.note: Echar un vistazo = to take a look.

examples.es: Te lo dejo para que me eches una mano.
examples.en: I'm leaving it with you so that you give me a hand.
examples.note: Echar una mano = to lend a hand. You help me.

contrast.es: Me quedo para echarte una mano.
contrast.en: I'm staying to give you a hand.
contrast.note: Same subject (I help) = infinitive. A different subject (you help) = que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto eche la carta, vuelvo.
examples.en: As soon as I post the letter, I'll come back.
examples.note: Echar una carta = to post a letter.

examples.es: En cuanto eches azúcar, remueve.
examples.en: As soon as you add sugar, stir.
examples.note: Echar = to add.

examples.es: En cuanto lo eche de menos, lo llamaré.
examples.en: As soon as I miss him, I'll call him.
examples.note: A future feeling, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: En cuanto lo echo de menos, lo llamo.
contrast.en: Whenever I miss him, I call him.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Echar is regular (eche, eches, echemos, echen) but sits inside lots of fixed expressions: echar de menos (Spain; extrañar in Latin America), echar una mano (help), echar un vistazo (take a look), echarse a + infinitive (burst out). Mind the reflexive: 'que se eche a perder' is not 'que eche a perder'.

title: caer

triggers.explanation: Puede que expresses possibility, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Puede que caiga una tormenta esta tarde.
examples.en: A storm may hit this afternoon.
examples.note: Caer is irregular: caiga, like caigo.

examples.es: Puede que caigamos en la trampa.
examples.en: We may fall into the trap.
examples.note: Caer en la trampa = to fall for the trap.

examples.es: Puede que te caiga bien mi hermano.
examples.en: You might like my brother.
examples.note: Caer bien = to make a good impression.

contrast.es: Seguro que te cae bien mi hermano.
contrast.en: You're sure to like my brother.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Puede que = possibility (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Sadness about something is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me da pena que caigas enfermo.
examples.en: It saddens me that you're falling ill.
examples.note: Caer enfermo = to fall ill.

examples.es: Me da pena que le caiga mal a tanta gente.
examples.en: It saddens me that so many people don't like him.
examples.note: Caer mal = to give a bad impression.

examples.es: Me da pena que no te caiga bien mi hermano.
examples.en: It saddens me that you don't like my brother.
examples.note: Caer bien works like gustar: the person liked is the subject.

contrast.es: Veo que no te cae bien mi hermano.
contrast.en: I see you don't like my brother.
contrast.note: Veo que states a fact (indicative). Me da pena que reacts (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Sujeta la escalera para que no me caiga.
examples.en: Hold the ladder so I don't fall.
examples.note: Caerse = to fall over.

examples.es: Ata los libros para que no se caigan.
examples.en: Tie the books together so they don't fall.
examples.note: Plural subject: caigan.

examples.es: Te agarro bien para que no te caigas.
examples.en: I'm holding you tight so that you don't fall.
examples.note: A purpose clause with a different subject.

contrast.es: Me agarro bien para no caerme.
contrast.en: I'm holding on tight so as not to fall.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Caer is irregular: caiga, caigas, caigamos, caigan, never 'caya'. 'Me cae bien' is about impressions and works like gustar: 'que te caiga bien'. Caerse (to fall over) needs the reflexive: 'que no te caigas'.

title: sentar vs sentarse

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quiero que te sientes a mi lado.
examples.en: I want you to sit next to me.
examples.note: Sentarse changes e→ie: sientes, not 'sentas'.

examples.es: Quiero que se sienten en silencio.
examples.en: I want them to sit down in silence.
examples.note: Ellos form: sienten.

examples.es: Quiero que te sientes aquí, junto a la ventana.
examples.en: I want you to sit here, next to the window.
examples.note: Te sientes (sentarse subjunctive) looks like te sientes (sentirse indicative).

contrast.es: Quiero que te sientas cómodo aquí.
contrast.en: I want you to feel comfortable here.
contrast.note: Te sientas = sentirse subjunctive (feel). Te sientes = sentarse subjunctive (sit). The vowels swap.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te sientes, abre el libro.
examples.en: When you sit down, open your book.
examples.note: Future moment, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando se sienten todos, empezamos.
examples.en: When everybody has sat down, we'll start.
examples.note: Todos is plural, so sienten.

examples.es: Cuando te sientes, verás mejor.
examples.en: When you sit down, you'll see better.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando te sientas, ves mejor.
contrast.en: Whenever you sit down, you see better.
contrast.note: Te sientas is here the indicative of sentarse: a habit.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dejo la silla libre para que te sientes.
examples.en: I'm leaving the chair free so you can sit down.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Mueve el bolso para que se siente la señora.
examples.en: Move your bag so the lady can sit down.
examples.note: Third person singular: siente.

examples.es: Pon más sillas para que se sienten todos.
examples.en: Put out more chairs so that everyone can sit down.
examples.note: Different subjects.

contrast.es: Pon más sillas para sentarnos todos.
contrast.en: Put out more chairs so we can all sit down.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Sentarse has e→ie in the subjunctive: me siente, te sientes, se siente, nos sentemos, se sienten. The trap is that 'te sientes' (sentarse subjunctive) is identical to 'te sientes' (sentirse indicative), while 'te sientas' is the other way round. And non-reflexive 'sentar' also means to suit: 'que te siente bien'.

title: seguir

triggers.explanation: Saying something is needed is a judgement about what should happen, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hace falta que sigas las instrucciones.
examples.en: You need to follow the instructions.
examples.note: Seguir = to follow. E→i stem: sigas.

examples.es: Hace falta que sigamos adelante.
examples.en: We need to keep going.
examples.note: Seguir adelante = to carry on.

examples.es: Hace falta que sigas estudiando para aprobar.
examples.en: You need to keep studying to pass.
examples.note: Seguir + gerund = to keep doing.

contrast.es: Sigues estudiando para aprobar.
contrast.en: You keep studying to pass.
contrast.note: A plain fact uses the indicative. A necessity uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubt means you don't take the statement as fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudo que siga lloviendo mañana.
examples.en: I doubt it'll still be raining tomorrow.
examples.note: Seguir + gerund = to still be doing.

examples.es: Dudo que sigan trabajando aquí.
examples.en: I doubt they're still working here.
examples.note: Ellos form: sigan.

examples.es: Dudo que siga vivo.
examples.en: I doubt he's still alive.
examples.note: Seguir + adjective = to still be.

contrast.es: No dudo que sigue vivo.
contrast.en: I don't doubt he's still alive.
contrast.note: Dudar takes the subjunctive. No dudar expresses certainty, so the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something not established as true.

examples.es: Aunque siga lloviendo, saldremos.
examples.en: Even if it's still raining, we'll go out.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Aunque sigas enfadado, ven a la cena.
examples.en: Even if you're still angry, come to the dinner.
examples.note: Seguir enfadado = to still be angry.

examples.es: Aunque siga sin entenderlo, lo intentaré.
examples.en: Even if I still don't understand it, I'll try.
examples.note: Seguir sin + infinitive = to still not.

contrast.es: Aunque sigo sin entenderlo, lo intento.
contrast.en: Although I still don't understand it, I'm trying.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Seguir has an e→i stem change and drops the u before a: siga, sigas, sigamos, sigan, never 'segua' or 'seguga'. Seguir + gerund = keep doing ('que sigas estudiando'), seguir + adjective = still be ('siga vivo'), seguir a = follow someone.

title: esperar

triggers.explanation: Saying what is preferable is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es preferible que esperes en el coche.
examples.en: It's better that you wait in the car.
examples.note: Esperar = to wait. Regular: esperes.

examples.es: Es preferible que esperemos a mañana.
examples.en: It's better that we wait until tomorrow.
examples.note: Esperar a = to wait until.

examples.es: Es preferible que no esperes nada de ellos.
examples.en: It's better that you don't expect anything from them.
examples.note: Esperar here = to expect.

contrast.es: Es evidente que no esperas nada de ellos.
contrast.en: It's obvious you don't expect anything from them.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es preferible judges what's better (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Asking someone to do something is a request, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te pido que esperes aquí.
examples.en: I ask you to wait here.
examples.note: Different subjects, so que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Te pido que esperemos juntos.
examples.en: I ask that we wait together.
examples.note: Nosotros includes the speaker.

examples.es: Te pido que no esperes un milagro.
examples.en: I'm asking you not to expect a miracle.
examples.note: Esperar un milagro = to hope for a miracle.

contrast.es: No esperas un milagro.
contrast.en: You don't expect a miracle.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A request uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando esperes el autobús, usa el banco.
examples.en: When you wait for the bus, use the bench.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando esperemos los resultados, estaremos nerviosos.
examples.en: When we're waiting for the results, we'll be nervous.
examples.note: Esperar + direct object = to wait for.

examples.es: Cuando esperes un hijo, todo cambiará.
examples.en: When you're expecting a baby, everything will change.
examples.note: Esperar un hijo = to be pregnant.

contrast.es: Cuando esperas un hijo, todo cambia.
contrast.en: When you're expecting a baby, everything changes.
contrast.note: A general truth uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Esperar is regular (espere, esperes, esperemos, esperen) but has two meanings, wait and hope or expect. 'Espero que' (I hope) takes the subjunctive, and 'esperar a que' (wait until) also does, with the subjunctive on the next verb. Esperar a alguien needs the personal a.

title: conseguir

triggers.explanation: Wishing something for someone is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Deseo que consigas el trabajo.
examples.en: I hope you get the job.
examples.note: Conseguir = to get. E→i stem: consigas.

examples.es: Deseo que consigamos un buen precio.
examples.en: I hope we get a good price.
examples.note: Nosotros: consigamos, with the i.

examples.es: Deseo que consigas aprobar el examen.
examples.en: I hope you manage to pass the exam.
examples.note: Conseguir + infinitive = to manage to.

contrast.es: Sé que consigues aprobar el examen.
contrast.en: I know you manage to pass the exam.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Desear expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Saying something isn't certain removes it from fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No es seguro que consiga entradas.
examples.en: It's not certain I'll get tickets.
examples.note: Entradas = tickets (Spain). In Latin America: boletos.

examples.es: No es seguro que consigan el permiso.
examples.en: It's not certain they'll get the permit.
examples.note: Ellos form: consigan.

examples.es: No es seguro que consigamos llegar a tiempo.
examples.en: It's not certain we'll manage to arrive on time.
examples.note: Conseguir + infinitive = to manage to.

contrast.es: Es seguro que conseguimos llegar a tiempo.
contrast.en: It's certain we manage to arrive on time.
contrast.note: Es seguro que asserts a fact (indicative). No es seguro que denies it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hago todo para que consigas tus sueños.
examples.en: I'm doing everything so you achieve your dreams.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Te ayudo para que consigas el puesto.
examples.en: I'm helping you so you get the position.
examples.note: Conseguir un puesto = to land a position.

examples.es: Trabajo para que consigamos la casa.
examples.en: I'm working so that we can get the house.
examples.note: Purpose with a different subject than the speaker.

contrast.es: Trabajo para conseguir la casa.
contrast.en: I'm working to get the house.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Conseguir has e→i and g (not gu) before a: consiga, consigas, consigamos, consigan, never 'consigua'. Conseguir + infinitive means manage to, so it says you succeeded, unlike poder: 'consigo hacerlo' vs 'puedo hacerlo'. 'Conseguir que' + subjunctive means to get someone to do something.

title: crear vs creer

triggers.explanation: Calling something fundamental is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es fundamental que crees buenos hábitos.
examples.en: It's essential that you create good habits.
examples.note: Crear's subjunctive is crees: the vowels differ from creer's creas.

examples.es: Es fundamental que crean en sí mismos.
examples.en: It's essential that they believe in themselves.
examples.note: Creer en = to believe in. Creer's subjunctive is crean.

examples.es: Es fundamental que creas en tu proyecto.
examples.en: It's essential that you believe in your project.
examples.note: Creas = creer subjunctive (believe).

contrast.es: Es fundamental que crees una empresa.
contrast.en: It's essential that you create a company.
contrast.note: One letter changes the meaning: creas = believe, crees = create.

triggers.explanation: Saying something is unlikely means it isn't a fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No es probable que cree problemas.
examples.en: It's unlikely that he'll create problems.
examples.note: Cree here is crear's subjunctive, not creer's indicative.

examples.es: No es probable que crea esa historia.
examples.en: It's unlikely that he'll believe that story.
examples.note: Crea here is creer's subjunctive.

examples.es: No es probable que ella cree una empresa este año.
examples.en: It's unlikely that she'll start a company this year.
examples.note: Crear una empresa = to set up a company.

contrast.es: Es seguro que ella crea una empresa este año.
contrast.en: It's certain that she'll start a company this year.
contrast.note: Es seguro que takes the indicative. No es probable que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando crees el archivo, guárdalo.
examples.en: When you create the file, save it.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando creas en ti mismo, todo cambiará.
examples.en: When you believe in yourself, everything will change.
examples.note: Creer en ti = to believe in yourself.

examples.es: Cuando cree la cuenta, te mando la contraseña.
examples.en: When I create the account, I'll send you the password.
examples.note: A future moment, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando crea una cuenta, siempre me manda la contraseña.
contrast.en: Whenever she creates an account, she always sends me the password.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative: crea is crear's indicative.

tricky: Crear's subjunctive is cree, crees, cree; creer's is crea, creas, crea. The vowels swap, so 'espero que crees' means I hope you create, while 'espero que creas' means I hope you believe. Cree is also creer's indicative (él cree), so context decides.

title: quedar vs quedarse

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá me quede tiempo.
examples.en: I hope I have some time left.
examples.note: Quedar = to be left. Me quede: time remains for me.

examples.es: Ojalá te quedes en Madrid un año más.
examples.en: I hope you stay in Madrid another year.
examples.note: Quedarse = to stay.

examples.es: Ojalá nos queden entradas.
examples.en: I hope there are tickets left for us.
examples.note: Quedar works like gustar: the tickets are the subject.

contrast.es: Nos quedan entradas.
contrast.en: We have tickets left.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A hope uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Llámame para que quedemos.
examples.en: Call me so that we arrange to meet.
examples.note: Quedar = to arrange to meet.

examples.es: Guarda un trozo para que me quede algo.
examples.en: Keep a piece so that I have something left.
examples.note: Quedar algo = something is left.

examples.es: Cómprate la talla grande para que te quede bien.
examples.en: Buy the large size so that it fits you well.
examples.note: Quedar bien = to fit or suit.

contrast.es: Esta talla te queda bien.
contrast.en: This size fits you well.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A purpose uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando quedemos, te cuento todo.
examples.en: When we meet up, I'll tell you everything.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te quedes sin gasolina, avísame.
examples.en: When you run out of petrol, let me know.
examples.note: Quedarse sin = to run out of.

examples.es: Cuando se quede solo, llorará.
examples.en: When he's left alone, he'll cry.
examples.note: Quedarse solo = to be left alone.

contrast.es: Cuando se queda solo, llora.
contrast.en: When he's left alone, he cries.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Quedar and quedarse are both regular (quede, quedes, quedemos). The -se changes the meaning: 'que quedemos' (that we arrange to meet) vs 'que nos quedemos' (that we stay). Quedar alone also means to be left or to fit, and works like gustar: 'que te quede bien'.

title: volverse vs hacerse (become)

triggers.explanation: Worry is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me preocupa que te vuelvas cínico.
examples.en: I'm worried you'll become cynical.
examples.note: Volverse + adjective = to become (a deep change).

examples.es: Me preocupa que se haga tarde.
examples.en: I'm worried it's getting late.
examples.note: Hacerse tarde = to get late (impersonal).

examples.es: Me preocupa que se vuelva loco.
examples.en: I'm worried he'll go mad.
examples.note: Volverse loco = to go mad.

contrast.es: Veo que se vuelve loco.
contrast.en: I see he's going mad.
contrast.note: Veo que states a fact (indicative). Me preocupa que reacts (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te hagas mayor, lo entenderás.
examples.en: When you grow up, you'll understand.
examples.note: Hacerse mayor = to grow up.

examples.es: Cuando se vuelva loco, no habrá quien lo pare.
examples.en: When he goes mad, nobody will be able to stop him.
examples.note: Volverse loco: a change that isn't chosen.

examples.es: Cuando te hagas rico, no te olvides de mí.
examples.en: When you get rich, don't forget me.
examples.note: Hacerse rico = to become rich (through effort).

contrast.es: Cuando te haces rico, te olvidas de todos.
contrast.en: When you get rich, you forget everyone.
contrast.note: A general truth uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something not established as true.

examples.es: Aunque me haga rico, seguiré aquí.
examples.en: Even if I get rich, I'll stay here.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Aunque se vuelva famoso, no cambiará.
examples.en: Even if he becomes famous, he won't change.
examples.note: Volverse famoso = to become famous.

examples.es: Aunque se haga vegetariano, seguirá comiendo queso.
examples.en: Even if he becomes vegetarian, he'll keep eating cheese.
examples.note: Hacerse + belief or profession = a deliberate choice.

contrast.es: Aunque se hizo vegetariano, sigue comiendo queso.
contrast.en: Although he became vegetarian, he keeps eating cheese.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Hacerse is a change you drive (se haga rico, médico, vegetariano), and volverse is a deeper, often unwelcome change (se vuelva loco, cínico). Both need the reflexive: 'que te hagas', 'que te vuelvas'. Haga is irregular, and vuelva has o→ue except volvamos.

title: dejar de vs parar

triggers.explanation: Calling something essential is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es imprescindible que dejes de fumar.
examples.en: It's essential that you quit smoking.
examples.note: Dejar de + infinitive = to quit for good.

examples.es: Es imprescindible que pares un momento.
examples.en: It's essential that you stop for a moment.
examples.note: Parar = to stop (often temporarily).

examples.es: Es imprescindible que pares de correr un momento.
examples.en: It's essential that you stop running for a moment.
examples.note: Parar de = to stop an action, maybe only for now. Dejar de would mean quitting.

contrast.es: Es evidente que dejas de correr.
contrast.en: It's obvious you're giving up running.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es imprescindible judges what's necessary (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando dejes de llorar, hablamos.
examples.en: When you stop crying, we'll talk.
examples.note: Dejar de llorar = to stop crying.

examples.es: Cuando pare de llover, salimos.
examples.en: When it stops raining, we'll go out.
examples.note: Parar de llover = to stop raining. Dejar de llover also works.

examples.es: Cuando deje de fumar, me sentiré mejor.
examples.en: When I quit smoking, I'll feel better.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando deja de fumar, se siente mejor.
contrast.en: Whenever he stops smoking, he feels better.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te lo digo para que dejes de preocuparte.
examples.en: I'm telling you so that you stop worrying.
examples.note: Dejar de + infinitive = to stop.

examples.es: Dale el biberón para que pare de llorar.
examples.en: Give him the bottle so that he stops crying.
examples.note: Parar de llorar = to stop crying.

examples.es: Se lo explico para que dejemos de discutir.
examples.en: I'm explaining it to him so that we stop arguing.
examples.note: Dejar de discutir = to stop arguing.

contrast.es: Se lo explico para dejar de discutir.
contrast.en: I'm explaining it to him to stop arguing (myself).
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Dejar de + infinitive means to quit, while parar de means to stop (often just for now). Both are regular: deje, pare. Keep the de: 'que dejes de fumar', because 'que dejes fumar' would not mean quit, it would mean something like 'that you allow smoking'.

title: acabar vs terminar

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hasn't happened yet.

examples.es: Hazlo antes de que acabe el día.
examples.en: Do it before the day ends.
examples.note: Acabar = to end. Regular: acabe.

examples.es: Salgamos antes de que termine la película.
examples.en: Let's leave before the film ends.
examples.note: Terminar = to finish.

examples.es: Llegaremos antes de que termine la película.
examples.en: We'll arrive before the film ends.
examples.note: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Llegamos después de que terminó la película.
contrast.en: We arrived after the film ended.
contrast.note: Después de que with a completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Hoping for something involves a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Espero que termines pronto.
examples.en: I hope you finish soon.
examples.note: Terminar = to finish an activity.

examples.es: Espero que acabemos esto hoy.
examples.en: I hope we finish this today.
examples.note: Acabar = to finish (often interchangeable with terminar).

examples.es: Espero que no acabe mal esta historia.
examples.en: I hope this story doesn't end badly.
examples.note: Acabar mal = to end badly.

contrast.es: Sé que acaba mal esta historia.
contrast.en: I know this story ends badly.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Esperar expresses a hope (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Quizás expresses doubt, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quizás termine antes de lo previsto.
examples.en: Maybe I'll finish earlier than planned.
examples.note: Quizás + subjunctive = genuine doubt.

examples.es: Quizás acabemos tarde.
examples.en: Maybe we'll finish late.
examples.note: Nosotros form: acabemos.

examples.es: Quizás acabe en la cárcel.
examples.en: Maybe he'll end up in jail.
examples.note: Acabar en = to end up in.

contrast.es: Seguro que acaba en la cárcel.
contrast.en: He's sure to end up in jail.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Quizás = doubt (subjunctive).

tricky: Acabar and terminar are both regular (acabe, termine). The catches are the patterns: acabar de + infinitive means 'just did' (acabo de comer), acabar + gerund means to end up (acabé durmiendo), and acabar con means to put an end to. Acabar mal or bien works like terminar mal or bien.

title: soler vs acostumbrarse

triggers.explanation: Doubt means you don't take the statement as fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudo que suela llegar tarde.
examples.en: I doubt he usually arrives late.
examples.note: Soler + infinitive = to usually do. O→ue: suela.

examples.es: Dudo que suelan salir a cenar.
examples.en: I doubt they usually go out for dinner.
examples.note: Ellos form: suelan.

examples.es: Dudo que suela ir al gimnasio.
examples.en: I doubt he usually goes to the gym.
examples.note: Soler is rare in the subjunctive but exists.

contrast.es: No dudo que suele ir al gimnasio.
contrast.en: I don't doubt he usually goes to the gym.
contrast.note: Dudar takes the subjunctive. No dudar expresses certainty, so the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Calling something good is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es bueno que te acostumbres al frío.
examples.en: It's good that you get used to the cold.
examples.note: Acostumbrarse a = to get used to.

examples.es: Es bueno que nos acostumbremos a madrugar.
examples.en: It's good that we get used to getting up early.
examples.note: Acostumbrarse a + infinitive.

examples.es: Es bueno que se acostumbren a vivir solos.
examples.en: It's good that they get used to living alone.
examples.note: Acostumbrarse is reflexive and takes a.

contrast.es: Es evidente que se acostumbran a vivir solos.
contrast.en: It's obvious they're getting used to living alone.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es bueno judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something not established as true.

examples.es: Aunque me acostumbre al ruido, prefiero el silencio.
examples.en: Even if I get used to the noise, I prefer silence.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Aunque no te acostumbres, tienes que seguir.
examples.en: Even if you don't get used to it, you have to carry on.
examples.note: Reflexive: te acostumbres.

examples.es: Aunque suela salir temprano, hoy se queda.
examples.en: Even if he usually leaves early, today he's staying.
examples.note: Soler + infinitive = to usually do.

contrast.es: Aunque suele salir temprano, hoy se queda.
contrast.en: Although he usually leaves early, today he's staying.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Soler is defective: it has no future or conditional, and the subjunctive suela, suelas, suelan is rare but real. It has o→ue except nosotros (solamos), and always takes an infinitive. Acostumbrarse always needs a (+ noun or infinitive) and the reflexive: 'que te acostumbres a ello'.

title: darse cuenta vs realizar

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá te des cuenta a tiempo.
examples.en: I hope you realise in time.
examples.note: Darse cuenta = to realise. Dar is irregular: des.

examples.es: Ojalá nos demos cuenta de nuestro error.
examples.en: I hope we realise our mistake.
examples.note: Nosotros: demos.

examples.es: Ojalá se dé cuenta de lo que pasa.
examples.en: I hope he realises what's happening.
examples.note: Dé takes an accent here.

contrast.es: Se da cuenta de lo que pasa.
contrast.en: He realises what's happening.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A hope uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te lo repito para que te des cuenta.
examples.en: I'm repeating it so that you realise.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Dame el contrato para que realice los cambios.
examples.en: Give me the contract so I can make the changes.
examples.note: Realizar = to carry out, not to realise. Z→c before e.

examples.es: Se lo repito para que se dé cuenta de su error.
examples.en: I'm repeating it to him so that he realises his mistake.
examples.note: Purpose, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Se lo repito porque no se da cuenta de su error.
contrast.en: I'm repeating it to him because he doesn't realise his mistake.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando realices el pago, avísame.
examples.en: When you make the payment, let me know.
examples.note: Realizar un pago = to make a payment.

examples.es: Cuando realicemos la compra, guarda el recibo.
examples.en: When we make the purchase, keep the receipt.
examples.note: Realizar = to carry out.

examples.es: Cuando realices el pedido, recibirás un correo.
examples.en: When you place the order, you'll receive an email.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando realizas el pedido, recibes un correo.
contrast.en: When you place the order, you receive an email.
contrast.note: A general rule uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Darse cuenta de uses dar: me dé, te des, se dé (with the accent), nos demos, se den cuenta. Realizar (z→c: realice) means to carry out, not to realise, a classic false friend: 'que realices el pago' (make it), never 'que realices tu error'.

title: asistir vs atender

triggers.explanation: Saying something is obligatory is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es obligatorio que asistas a la reunión.
examples.en: It's mandatory that you attend the meeting.
examples.note: Asistir a = to attend. Regular: asistas.

examples.es: Es obligatorio que asistamos al curso.
examples.en: It's mandatory that we attend the course.
examples.note: Asistir a + event.

examples.es: Es obligatorio que atiendan a todos los clientes.
examples.en: It's mandatory that they serve every customer.
examples.note: Atender = to serve or look after. E→ie: atiendan.

contrast.es: Es evidente que atienden a todos los clientes.
contrast.en: It's obvious they serve every customer.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es obligatorio judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Asking someone to act is a request, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Pídele que asista a la boda.
examples.en: Ask him to go to the wedding.
examples.note: Asistir a = to attend.

examples.es: Pídele que atienda el teléfono.
examples.en: Ask her to answer the phone.
examples.note: Atender el teléfono = to answer the phone.

examples.es: Pídele que atienda a los niños mientras estoy fuera.
examples.en: Ask him to look after the children while I'm out.
examples.note: Atender a = to take care of, to serve.

contrast.es: Sé que atiende a los niños mientras estoy fuera.
contrast.en: I know he looks after the children while I'm out.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Pedir expresses a request (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando asistas a la boda, llévale un regalo.
examples.en: When you go to the wedding, take her a present.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando atiendan mi pedido, te aviso.
examples.en: When they deal with my order, I'll let you know.
examples.note: Atender un pedido = to process an order.

examples.es: Cuando asista a la conferencia, tomaré notas.
examples.en: When I attend the conference, I'll take notes.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando asisto a una conferencia, tomo notas.
contrast.en: Whenever I attend a conference, I take notes.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Asistir is regular (asista, asistamos) but atender has e→ie: atienda, atiendas, atiendan, with atendamos for nosotros. Asistir a means attend, atender means serve or look after, and neither is the everyday 'help': for that use ayudar.

title: soportar vs apoyar

triggers.explanation: Reacting with incomprehension is an emotional response, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No entiendo que apoyes a ese equipo.
examples.en: I don't understand how you support that team.
examples.note: Apoyar = to support. Regular: apoyes.

examples.es: No entiendo que soportes tanto ruido.
examples.en: I don't understand how you put up with so much noise.
examples.note: Soportar = to put up with, not to support.

examples.es: No entiendo que lo soportes.
examples.en: I don't understand how you stand him.
examples.note: Soportar a alguien = to put up with someone.

contrast.es: Veo que lo soportas.
contrast.en: I see you put up with him.
contrast.note: Veo que states a fact (indicative). No entiendo que reacts (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Calling something fair is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es justo que apoyemos a nuestros amigos.
examples.en: It's fair that we support our friends.
examples.note: Apoyar a = to support someone.

examples.es: Es justo que apoyen a las familias que lo necesitan.
examples.en: It's fair that they support the families who need it.
examples.note: Ellos form: apoyen.

examples.es: Es justo que apoyes a tu hermano.
examples.en: It's fair that you back your brother.
examples.note: A moral judgement, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Es evidente que apoyas a tu hermano.
contrast.en: It's obvious you back your brother.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es justo judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Habla con ellos para que te apoyen.
examples.en: Talk to them so that they support you.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Refuerza la pared para que soporte el peso.
examples.en: Reinforce the wall so that it holds the weight.
examples.note: Soportar also means to bear a physical load.

examples.es: Refuerza la estantería para que soporte más peso.
examples.en: Reinforce the shelf so that it can bear more weight.
examples.note: Soportar = to withstand a load.

contrast.es: Ahora la estantería soporta más peso.
contrast.en: The shelf now bears more weight.
contrast.note: A fact uses the indicative. A purpose uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Soportar means to put up with or to bear a load, and never to support someone: that's apoyar ('que apoyes a tu equipo', 'que soportes el ruido'). Both are regular (soporte, apoye). Soportar is also used for software that supports a format.

title: introducir vs presentar

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quiero que me presentes a tu hermana.
examples.en: I want you to introduce me to your sister.
examples.note: Presentar a alguien = to introduce someone.

examples.es: Quiero que introduzcas la tarjeta en la ranura.
examples.en: I want you to insert the card into the slot.
examples.note: Introducir = to insert. Irregular: introduzcas, with -zc-.

examples.es: Quiero que presentes tu proyecto el lunes.
examples.en: I want you to present your project on Monday.
examples.note: Presentar = to present. Different subject from the speaker.

contrast.es: Quiero presentar mi proyecto el lunes.
contrast.en: I want to present my project on Monday.
contrast.note: Same subject = infinitive. A different subject = que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando me presentes a tu madre, estaré nervioso.
examples.en: When you introduce me to your mother, I'll be nervous.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando introduzcas los datos, pulsa intro.
examples.en: When you've entered the data, press enter.
examples.note: Introducir datos = to enter data.

examples.es: Cuando introduzcas los datos, el sistema los validará.
examples.en: When you enter the data, the system will validate it.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando introduces los datos, el sistema los valida.
contrast.en: Whenever you enter the data, the system validates it.
contrast.note: A routine uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: A possibility isn't a fact, so the subjunctive is needed.

examples.es: Es posible que presente el informe mañana.
examples.en: It's possible he'll present the report tomorrow.
examples.note: Regular: presente.

examples.es: Es posible que introduzcan cambios.
examples.en: It's possible they'll introduce changes.
examples.note: Introducir cambios = to bring in changes.

examples.es: Es posible que presenten la dimisión.
examples.en: It's possible they'll hand in their resignation.
examples.note: Presentar la dimisión = to resign formally.

contrast.es: Seguro que presentan la dimisión.
contrast.en: They're sure to hand in their resignation.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Es posible que = possibility (subjunctive).

tricky: Introducir is irregular with -zc-: introduzca, introduzcas, introduzcamos, introduzcan, like conducir. Presentar is regular (presente). Introducir is to insert or bring in, but presentar is to introduce a person: 'que me presentes a tu madre', never 'que me introduzcas'.

title: pretender vs fingir

triggers.explanation: Calling something ridiculous is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es ridículo que finjas estar enfermo.
examples.en: It's ridiculous that you pretend to be ill.
examples.note: Fingir = to pretend. G→j before a: finjas, never 'fingas'.

examples.es: Es ridículo que pretendan cambiar las reglas.
examples.en: It's ridiculous that they expect to change the rules.
examples.note: Pretender = to aim to, to expect to.

examples.es: Es ridículo que pretenda convencerme.
examples.en: It's ridiculous that he's trying to convince me.
examples.note: Pretender + infinitive = to try / aim to.

contrast.es: Es evidente que pretende convencerme.
contrast.en: It's obvious he's trying to convince me.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es ridículo judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something not established as true.

examples.es: Aunque finja, se le nota.
examples.en: Even if he pretends, it shows.
examples.note: Fingir with no object = to put it on.

examples.es: Aunque pretendas lo contrario, no te creo.
examples.en: Even if you claim the opposite, I don't believe you.
examples.note: Pretender here = to claim.

examples.es: Aunque pretendan ayudarnos, no confío en ellos.
examples.en: Even if they claim they want to help us, I don't trust them.
examples.note: Pretender + infinitive = to aim to.

contrast.es: Aunque pretenden ayudarnos, no confío en ellos.
contrast.en: Although they say they want to help us, I don't trust them.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

triggers.explanation: Saying something isn't needed is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No hace falta que finjas.
examples.en: You don't need to pretend.
examples.note: No hace falta que + subjunctive.

examples.es: No hace falta que pretendas ser perfecto.
examples.en: You don't need to aim to be perfect.
examples.note: Pretender ser = to aim to be, not to pretend to be.

examples.es: No hace falta que finjas alegría.
examples.en: You don't need to fake happiness.
examples.note: Fingir alegría = to fake happiness.

contrast.es: Siempre finges alegría.
contrast.en: You always fake happiness.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. Denying a need uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Pretender is a false friend: it means to aim, intend or claim, not to pretend, which is fingir. Pretender is regular (pretenda). Fingir changes g→j before a: finja, finjas, finjamos, never 'finga'. 'No pretendo que lo entiendas' = I don't expect you to understand.

title: avergonzado vs embarazada

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que esté embarazada.
examples.en: I don't think she's pregnant.
examples.note: Estar embarazada = to be pregnant, never embarrassed.

examples.es: No creo que se avergüence de su familia.
examples.en: I don't think he's ashamed of his family.
examples.note: Avergonzarse has o→üe: avergüence.

examples.es: No creo que esté embarazada; solo está avergonzada.
examples.en: I don't think she's pregnant; she's just embarrassed.
examples.note: Embarazada means pregnant, not embarrassed (avergonzada): a false friend.

contrast.es: Creo que está embarazada.
contrast.en: I think she's pregnant.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Calling something understandable is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es comprensible que te dé vergüenza.
examples.en: It's understandable that you feel embarrassed.
examples.note: Dar vergüenza works like gustar: me da vergüenza.

examples.es: Es comprensible que se avergüence.
examples.en: It's understandable that he feels ashamed.
examples.note: Reflexive avergonzarse: se avergüence.

examples.es: Es comprensible que esté avergonzada después de aquello.
examples.en: It's understandable that she's embarrassed after that.
examples.note: Estar avergonzada = to be embarrassed.

contrast.es: Es evidente que está avergonzada después de aquello.
contrast.en: It's obvious she's embarrassed after that.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es comprensible judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te avergüences, cuéntamelo.
examples.en: When you feel ashamed, tell me.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te dé vergüenza, respira hondo.
examples.en: When you feel embarrassed, breathe deeply.
examples.note: Dar vergüenza works like gustar: vergüenza is the subject, so the third-person dé with its accent.

examples.es: Cuando esté embarazada, tendrá derecho a baja.
examples.en: When she's pregnant, she'll be entitled to leave.
examples.note: A future condition, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando está embarazada, tiene derecho a baja.
contrast.en: When she's pregnant, she is entitled to leave.
contrast.note: A general rule uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Embarazada means pregnant, never embarrassed; embarrassed is avergonzado/a or 'me da vergüenza'. Avergonzarse has o→üe with a diaeresis and z→c: me avergüence, nos avergoncemos. 'Dar vergüenza' works like gustar and has an accent on dé: 'que te dé vergüenza'.

title: conducir vs manejar

triggers.explanation: Calling something dangerous is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es peligroso que conduzcas cansado.
examples.en: It's dangerous for you to drive tired.
examples.note: Conducir has -zc-: conduzcas, never 'conduzas'.

examples.es: Es peligroso que manejes con lluvia.
examples.en: It's dangerous for you to drive in the rain.
examples.note: Manejar is the usual verb for driving in Latin America.

examples.es: Es peligroso que conduzcas sin gafas.
examples.en: It's dangerous for you to drive without glasses.
examples.note: A judgement about risk.

contrast.es: Sé que conduces sin gafas.
contrast.en: I know you drive without glasses.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Es peligroso que judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando conduzcas, usa el cinturón.
examples.en: When you drive, wear your seatbelt.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando maneje de noche, usaré gafas.
examples.en: When I drive at night, I'll wear glasses.
examples.note: Maneje is regular.

examples.es: Cuando conduzca por la ciudad, iré despacio.
examples.en: When I drive through the city, I'll go slowly.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando conduzco por la ciudad, voy despacio.
contrast.en: Whenever I drive through the city, I go slowly.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubt means you don't take the statement as fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudo que maneje bien.
examples.en: I doubt he drives well.
examples.note: Regular: maneje.

examples.es: Dudo que conduzcan tan rápido.
examples.en: I doubt they drive that fast.
examples.note: Ellos form: conduzcan.

examples.es: Dudo que conduzca ese camión.
examples.en: I doubt he drives that lorry.
examples.note: In Spain, camión; in Mexico, camión can mean bus.

contrast.es: No dudo que conduce ese camión.
contrast.en: I don't doubt he drives that lorry.
contrast.note: Dudar takes the subjunctive. No dudar expresses certainty, so the indicative.

tricky: Conducir is irregular with -zc-: conduzca, conduzcas, conduzcamos, conduzcan, never 'conduza'. Manejar is regular (maneje). The choice is regional: conducir is standard in Spain, manejar in most of Latin America, though both are understood everywhere.

title: probar vs intentar

triggers.explanation: Saying what is advisable is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es recomendable que intentes ir temprano.
examples.en: It's advisable that you try to go early.
examples.note: Intentar + infinitive = to try to. Regular: intentes.

examples.es: Es recomendable que pruebes el vino antes de comprarlo.
examples.en: It's advisable that you taste the wine before buying it.
examples.note: Probar has o→ue: pruebes, never 'probes'.

examples.es: Es recomendable que intentes hablar con ella.
examples.en: It's advisable that you try to talk to her.
examples.note: Intentar = to make an attempt. 'Probar hablar' isn't possible; it needs a (probar a hablar), so intentar is the standard choice.

contrast.es: Es obvio que intentas hablar con ella.
contrast.en: It's obvious you're trying to talk to her.
contrast.note: Es obvio states a fact (indicative). Es recomendable judges what's advisable (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Corta un trozo para que pruebe el queso.
examples.en: Cut a piece so that he can taste the cheese.
examples.note: Probar = to taste.

examples.es: Te invito para que pruebes el postre.
examples.en: I'm inviting you so that you try the dessert.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Hablo contigo para que intentes otra vez.
examples.en: I'm talking to you so that you try again.
examples.note: Different subjects.

contrast.es: Hablo contigo para intentarlo otra vez.
contrast.en: I'm talking to you to try again.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando pruebes el café, dime qué opinas.
examples.en: When you try the coffee, tell me what you think.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando intentes abrirla, hazlo con cuidado.
examples.en: When you try to open it, be careful.
examples.note: Intentar + infinitive.

examples.es: Cuando lo intentes de nuevo, tendrás más suerte.
examples.en: When you try again, you'll have more luck.
examples.note: A future attempt, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando lo intentas, siempre sale mal.
contrast.en: Whenever you try it, it always goes wrong.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Probar has an o→ue stem change (pruebe, pruebes, prueben) but probemos in nosotros, and intentar is regular (intente). Probar is to test, taste or try on, and intentar is to attempt, so say 'que intentes hablar', not 'que pruebes hablar' (in Spain 'probar a + infinitive' is possible).

title: mover vs mudarse

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá te mudes pronto.
examples.en: I hope you move soon.
examples.note: Mudarse = to move house. Reflexive: te mudes.

examples.es: Ojalá nos mudemos a una casa grande.
examples.en: I hope we move to a big house.
examples.note: Nosotros: nos mudemos.

examples.es: Ojalá se mueva la fila más rápido.
examples.en: I hope the queue moves faster.
examples.note: Moverse = to move or progress. O→ue: mueva.

contrast.es: La fila se mueve más rápido.
contrast.en: The queue is moving faster.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A hope uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hasn't happened yet.

examples.es: Avísame antes de que te mudes.
examples.en: Let me know before you move.
examples.note: Different subjects, so antes de que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Hablemos antes de que se mude.
examples.en: Let's talk before he moves out.
examples.note: Third person: se mude.

examples.es: Quita el mueble antes de que se mueva el camión.
examples.en: Take away the furniture before the lorry moves off.
examples.note: Moverse also means to move off.

contrast.es: Quité el mueble después de que se movió el camión.
contrast.en: I took away the furniture after the lorry moved off.
contrast.note: Después de que with a completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Likelihood isn't certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es probable que me mude en verano.
examples.en: I'll probably move in the summer.
examples.note: Mudarse = to move house.

examples.es: Es probable que muevan la reunión al jueves.
examples.en: It's likely they'll move the meeting to Thursday.
examples.note: Mover = to shift or reschedule. O→ue: muevan.

examples.es: Es probable que se mude a otra ciudad.
examples.en: It's likely he'll move to another city.
examples.note: Mudarse a = to move to.

contrast.es: Seguro que se muda a otra ciudad.
contrast.en: He's sure to move to another city.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Es probable que = likelihood (subjunctive).

tricky: Mover has o→ue: mueva, muevas, muevan, but movamos for nosotros. Mudarse is regular (me mude, te mudes). Mover is to shift something, moverse is to move about, and mudarse is to move house: 'que muevas la silla' vs 'que te mudes de casa'.

title: aprender vs enseñar

triggers.explanation: Calling something essential is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es esencial que aprendas de tus errores.
examples.en: It's essential that you learn from your mistakes.
examples.note: Aprender de = to learn from. Regular.

examples.es: Es esencial que enseñemos con el ejemplo.
examples.en: It's essential that we teach by example.
examples.note: Enseñar = to teach.

examples.es: Es esencial que aprenda a escuchar.
examples.en: It's essential that he learns to listen.
examples.note: Aprender a + infinitive = to learn to.

contrast.es: Es evidente que aprende a escuchar.
contrast.en: It's obvious that he's learning to listen.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es esencial judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto aprenda a nadar, iremos al mar.
examples.en: As soon as I learn to swim, we'll go to the sea.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto me enseñes la casa, decidimos.
examples.en: As soon as you show me the house, we'll decide.
examples.note: Enseñar = to show.

examples.es: En cuanto aprendas la lección, podrás salir.
examples.en: As soon as you learn the lesson, you'll be able to go out.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: En cuanto aprendes la lección, sales.
contrast.en: As soon as you learn the lesson, you go out.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Repetiré la lección para que aprendas.
examples.en: I'll repeat the lesson so that you learn.
examples.note: Para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Voy a la escuela para que me enseñen a nadar.
examples.en: I'm going to the school so that they teach me to swim.
examples.note: Enseñar a + infinitive = to teach to.

examples.es: Le pago para que me enseñe a tocar la guitarra.
examples.en: I pay him so that he teaches me to play the guitar.
examples.note: Purpose with a different subject.

contrast.es: Le pago porque me enseña a tocar la guitarra.
contrast.en: I pay him because he teaches me to play the guitar.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Aprender and enseñar are both regular (aprenda, enseñe), and the ñ stays. Enseñar covers both teach and show: 'que me enseñes inglés' (teach) vs 'que me enseñes tu casa' (show). Don't swap aprender and enseñar: the learner uses aprender, the teacher uses enseñar.

title: dar vs regalar

triggers.explanation: Calling something crazy is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es una locura que regales tanto dinero.
examples.en: It's crazy that you give away so much money.
examples.note: Regalar = to give for free. Regular: regales.

examples.es: Es una locura que me des este coche.
examples.en: It's crazy that you give me this car.
examples.note: Dar is irregular: des.

examples.es: Es una locura que le dé todo su dinero.
examples.en: It's crazy that he gives her all his money.
examples.note: Dé needs an accent.

contrast.es: Es cierto que le da todo su dinero.
contrast.en: It's true that he gives her all his money.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es una locura reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando regales algo, pon una nota.
examples.en: When you give a present, add a note.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando me des la respuesta, lo decidimos.
examples.en: When you give me the answer, we'll decide.
examples.note: Dar la respuesta = to give the answer.

examples.es: Cuando regales un libro, escribe una dedicatoria.
examples.en: When you give a book as a gift, write a dedication.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando regalas un libro, escribes una dedicatoria.
contrast.en: Whenever you give a book as a gift, you write a dedication.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que regale nada.
examples.en: I don't think he'll give anything.
examples.note: Regalar nada = to give nothing as a gift.

examples.es: No creo que nos den descuento.
examples.en: I don't think they'll give us a discount.
examples.note: Dar descuento = to give a discount.

examples.es: No creo que me regale nada: es muy tacaño.
examples.en: I don't think he'll give me anything: he's very stingy.
examples.note: Regalar = give with nothing in return.

contrast.es: Creo que me regala algo.
contrast.en: I think he gives me something.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Dar's subjunctive is dé (with an accent), des, dé, demos, den, and regalar is regular (regale). Regalar is to give as a gift, with nothing expected back, while dar is general giving. Native speakers prefer 'te regalo' over 'te doy un regalo'.

title: prestar vs pedir prestado

triggers.explanation: Fear is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me da miedo que prestes tu coche a cualquiera.
examples.en: I'm afraid you'll lend your car to anyone.
examples.note: Prestar = to lend. Regular: prestes.

examples.es: Me da miedo que pidas prestado tanto dinero.
examples.en: I'm afraid you'll borrow so much money.
examples.note: Pedir changes e→i: pidas.

examples.es: Me da miedo que pida prestado más dinero.
examples.en: I'm afraid he'll borrow more money.
examples.note: Pedir prestado = to borrow.

contrast.es: Sé que pide prestado más dinero.
contrast.en: I know he borrows more money.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Me da miedo que reacts (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Habla con él para que te preste la moto.
examples.en: Talk to him so that he lends you the motorbike.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Habla con ella para que nos preste la casa.
examples.en: Talk to her so that she lends us the house.
examples.note: Prestar la casa = to lend the house.

examples.es: Llámalo para que te preste el coche este fin de semana.
examples.en: Call him so that he lends you the car this weekend.
examples.note: The lender is the subject of the second clause.

contrast.es: Lo llamo para pedirle prestado el coche.
contrast.en: I'm calling him to borrow the car.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando pidas prestado algo, devuélvelo.
examples.en: When you borrow something, give it back.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te preste el coche, ten cuidado.
examples.en: When I lend you the car, be careful.
examples.note: Prestar = to lend.

examples.es: Cuando pidamos prestado dinero, firmaremos un papel.
examples.en: When we borrow money, we'll sign a paper.
examples.note: Pedir keeps e→i in nosotros: pidamos, never 'pedamos'.

contrast.es: Cuando pedimos prestado dinero, firmamos un papel.
contrast.en: Whenever we borrow money, we sign a paper.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Prestar is regular (preste), but pedir prestado carries pedir's e→i change: pida prestado, pidas, pidamos, pidan. 'Que me prestes' = that you lend me, and 'que me pidas prestado' = that you borrow from me. English 'borrow' and 'lend' mix easily, but Spanish keeps them apart.

title: llamar vs llamarse

triggers.explanation: Asking someone to do something is a request, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te pido que llames a tu madre.
examples.en: I ask you to call your mother.
examples.note: Llamar a = to phone or call someone.

examples.es: Te pido que me llames cuando llegues.
examples.en: I ask you to call me when you arrive.
examples.note: Me llames: you phone me. Llegues is also subjunctive after cuando.

examples.es: Te pido que me llames Ana, no señora.
examples.en: I ask you to call me Ana, not ma'am.
examples.note: Llamar + name = to address someone by a name.

contrast.es: Me llamo Ana.
contrast.en: My name is Ana.
contrast.note: Llamarse = to be named. Llamar = to call someone something.

triggers.explanation: When the person you describe doesn't exist, the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: No hay nadie que llame a esta hora.
examples.en: There's nobody who calls at this hour.
examples.note: Nadie = no such person, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No hay nadie que se llame así en mi clase.
examples.en: There's nobody called that in my class.
examples.note: Llamarse = to be called. Reflexive: se llame.

examples.es: No hay nadie que se llame Pancracio en el pueblo.
examples.en: There's nobody called Pancracio in the village.
examples.note: A non-existent person calls for the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Hay un chico que se llama Pancracio en el pueblo.
contrast.en: There's a boy called Pancracio in the village.
contrast.note: A person who exists takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando llames, pregunta por Marta.
examples.en: When you call, ask for Marta.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando me llames, ya estaré en casa.
examples.en: By the time you call me, I'll be home.
examples.note: Future event.

examples.es: Cuando te llame el médico, avísame.
examples.en: When the doctor calls you, let me know.
examples.note: A future call, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando te llama el médico, siempre me avisas.
