contrast.en: Whenever the doctor calls you, you always let me know.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Llamar is regular (llame, llames), and llamarse adds the pronoun: me llame, te llames, se llame, nos llamemos. The pronoun changes the meaning: 'que me llames' (that you phone me) vs 'que te llames' (that you be named). Llamar a + person = to phone someone.

title: levantar vs levantarse

triggers.explanation: Preferring that someone else act in a certain way is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Prefiero que te levantes temprano.
examples.en: I prefer that you get up early.
examples.note: Levantarse = to get up. Reflexive: te levantes.

examples.es: Prefiero que se levanten todos a la vez.
examples.en: I prefer that everyone gets up at the same time.
examples.note: Todos is plural, so se levanten.

examples.es: Prefiero que levantes al niño con cuidado.
examples.en: I prefer that you lift the child carefully.
examples.note: Levantar a alguien = to lift someone.

contrast.es: Prefiero que el niño se levante solo.
contrast.en: I prefer that the child gets up on his own.
contrast.note: Se levante = get up. Levantes = lift. The reflexive decides.

triggers.explanation: Hasta que about something not yet completed takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Espera hasta que se levante la niebla.
examples.en: Wait until the fog lifts.
examples.note: Levantarse also means to lift (of fog) or to rise.

examples.es: Quédate sentado hasta que se levanten los demás.
examples.en: Stay seated until the others get up.
examples.note: Ellos form: se levanten.

examples.es: Descansa hasta que te levantes sin dolor.
examples.en: Rest until you can get up without pain.
examples.note: Future / unfinished event = subjunctive.

contrast.es: Descansé hasta que me levanté sin dolor.
contrast.en: I rested until I could get up without pain.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te pongo la alarma para que te levantes a tiempo.
examples.en: I'll set the alarm for you so that you get up on time.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Habla bajo para que no se levante el bebé.
examples.en: Speak quietly so that the baby doesn't get up.
examples.note: Se levante: the baby gets up.

examples.es: Ayúdame para que levantemos la mesa.
examples.en: Help me so that we lift the table.
examples.note: Levantar = to lift an object.

contrast.es: Ayúdame para levantar la mesa.
contrast.en: Help me to lift the table.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Levantar and levantarse are both regular (levante, levantes), but the reflexive decides the meaning: 'que levantes la caja' (lift it) vs 'que te levantes' (get up). Don't drop it: 'que me levante a las siete'. In many places 'levantar a alguien' also means to wake someone up.

title: ir vs irse

triggers.explanation: Not wanting something to happen is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No quiero que te vayas.
examples.en: I don't want you to leave.
examples.note: Irse = to leave. Reflexive: te vayas.

examples.es: No quiero que se vaya sin despedirse.
examples.en: I don't want him to leave without saying goodbye.
examples.note: Irse = to go away.

examples.es: No quiero que vayas a casa de Pedro.
examples.en: I don't want you to go to Pedro's house.
examples.note: Ir a = to go toward a place. No reflexive.

contrast.es: No quiero que te vayas de casa de Pedro.
contrast.en: I don't want you to leave Pedro's house.
contrast.note: Ir a = go to. Irse de = leave from.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te vayas, cierra la puerta.
examples.en: When you leave, close the door.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando vayamos al mercado, compra pan.
examples.en: When we go to the market, buy bread.
examples.note: Vayamos is the nosotros subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando vayas al médico, pregunta por el análisis.
examples.en: When you go to the doctor's, ask about the test.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando vas al médico, siempre preguntas.
contrast.en: Whenever you go to the doctor's, you always ask.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: A possibility isn't a fact, so the subjunctive is needed.

examples.es: Es posible que se vaya mañana.
examples.en: It's possible he'll leave tomorrow.
examples.note: Irse = to leave.

examples.es: Es posible que vayamos al cine.
examples.en: It's possible we'll go to the cinema.
examples.note: Ir a = go to.

examples.es: Es posible que nos vayamos de viaje.
examples.en: It's possible we'll go away on a trip.
examples.note: Irse de viaje = to go away on a trip.

contrast.es: Seguro que nos vamos de viaje.
contrast.en: We're sure to go away on a trip.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Es posible que = possibility (subjunctive).

tricky: Ir's subjunctive is vaya, vayas, vayamos, vayan, never 'vaye', and irse adds the pronoun: me vaya, te vayas, se vaya, nos vayamos. Ir a means to go toward and irse de means to leave. 'Let's go' is 'vámonos' (affirmative), but the negative is 'no nos vayamos'.

title: dormir vs dormirse

triggers.explanation: Hoping for something involves a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Espero que duermas bien.
examples.en: I hope you sleep well.
examples.note: Dormir has o→ue: duermas.

examples.es: Espero que no te duermas en la reunión.
examples.en: I hope you don't fall asleep in the meeting.
examples.note: Dormirse = to fall asleep. Reflexive: te duermas.

examples.es: Espero que se duerma pronto el bebé.
examples.en: I hope the baby falls asleep soon.
examples.note: Dormirse = to fall asleep. Dormir would mean to sleep.

contrast.es: Veo que se duerme pronto el bebé.
contrast.en: I see the baby falls asleep soon.
contrast.note: Veo que states a fact (indicative). Esperar expresses a hope (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hasn't happened yet.

examples.es: Dímelo antes de que me duerma.
examples.en: Tell me before I fall asleep.
examples.note: Different subjects, so antes de que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Hablemos antes de que duerman los niños.
examples.en: Let's talk before the children sleep.
examples.note: Ellos form with o→ue: duerman.

examples.es: Llámame antes de que se duerma el niño.
examples.en: Call me before the child falls asleep.
examples.note: The falling asleep hasn't happened yet.

contrast.es: Te llamé después de que se durmió el niño.
contrast.en: I called you after the child fell asleep.
contrast.note: Después de que with a completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando duermas, apaga el móvil.
examples.en: When you sleep, turn off your phone.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando se duerma, saldremos.
examples.en: When she falls asleep, we'll go out.
examples.note: Dormirse = to fall asleep.

examples.es: Cuando me duerma, no me despiertes.
examples.en: When I fall asleep, don't wake me.
examples.note: A future moment, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando me duermo, no me despierto con nada.
contrast.en: When I fall asleep, nothing wakes me.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Dormir changes o→ue in most forms and o→u in nosotros: duerma, duermas, durmamos, duerman. Dormirse is to fall asleep: 'que duermas' (that you sleep) vs 'que te duermas' (that you nod off). Durmamos (subjunctive) also works as 'let's sleep', while 'dormimos' is the indicative 'we sleep'.

title: estar de acuerdo vs acordar

triggers.explanation: Calling something important is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es importante que estemos de acuerdo.
examples.en: It's important that we agree.
examples.note: Estar de acuerdo = to agree (share an opinion).

examples.es: Es importante que acordemos un horario.
examples.en: It's important that we agree on a schedule.
examples.note: Acordar = to agree on / arrange. Nosotros keeps the o: acordemos.

examples.es: Es importante que acuerden los términos antes de firmar.
examples.en: It's important that they agree the terms before signing.
examples.note: Acordar has o→ue: acuerden.

contrast.es: Es obvio que acuerdan los términos antes de firmar.
contrast.en: It's obvious that they agree the terms before signing.
contrast.note: Es obvio states a fact (indicative). Es importante judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que esté de acuerdo.
examples.en: I don't think he agrees.
examples.note: Esté keeps its accent.

examples.es: No creo que estén de acuerdo con el plan.
examples.en: I don't think they agree with the plan.
examples.note: Estar de acuerdo con = to agree with.

examples.es: No creo que acuerden nada hoy.
examples.en: I don't think they'll agree anything today.
examples.note: Acordar = to reach an agreement.

contrast.es: Creo que acuerdan algo hoy.
contrast.en: I think they agree something today.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Habla con ella para que esté de acuerdo.
examples.en: Talk to her so that she agrees.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Habla con el vendedor para que acuerde un precio justo.
examples.en: Talk to the seller so that he agrees a fair price.
examples.note: Acordar un precio = to agree a price. Different subjects.

examples.es: Les escribo para que acuerden una fecha.
examples.en: I'm writing to them so that they agree a date.
examples.note: Different subjects.

contrast.es: Les escribo para acordar una fecha.
contrast.en: I'm writing to them to agree a date.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Estar de acuerdo needs the full phrase: esté de acuerdo, estén de acuerdo, with the accent on esté. Acordar has o→ue (acuerde, acuerden) but acordemos in nosotros. Don't mix up acordar (to agree, arrange) with acordarse (to remember): 'que acordemos' vs 'que nos acordemos'.

title: hacer falta vs necesitar

triggers.explanation: Puede que expresses possibility, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Puede que haga falta más tiempo.
examples.en: We may need more time.
examples.note: Hacer falta = to be needed. Haga is irregular.

examples.es: Puede que necesitemos ayuda.
examples.en: We may need help.
examples.note: Necesitar is regular, with the person as subject.

examples.es: Puede que me haga falta un abrigo.
examples.en: I may need a coat.
examples.note: With hacer falta, the thing needed is the subject: un abrigo.

contrast.es: Seguro que me hace falta un abrigo.
contrast.en: I definitely need a coat.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Puede que = possibility (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que necesite ayuda.
examples.en: I don't think he needs help.
examples.note: Necesitar + noun = to need.

examples.es: No creo que te hagan falta más libros.
examples.en: I don't think you need more books.
examples.note: Libros is plural, so hagan agrees with the thing needed.

examples.es: No creo que necesites tanto dinero.
examples.en: I don't think you need that much money.
examples.note: Necesitar puts you as the subject.

contrast.es: Creo que necesitas tanto dinero.
contrast.en: I think you need that much money.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando necesites algo, llámame.
examples.en: When you need something, call me.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te haga falta dinero, pídemelo.
examples.en: When you need money, ask me for it.
examples.note: Hacer falta works like gustar.

examples.es: Cuando necesite ayuda, la pediré.
examples.en: When I need help, I'll ask for it.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando necesito ayuda, la pido.
contrast.en: Whenever I need help, I ask for it.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Hacer falta works like gustar: the thing needed is the subject and agrees ('que te haga falta tiempo', 'que te hagan falta libros'), and haga is irregular. Necesitar is regular (necesite) and puts you as the subject: 'que necesites tiempo'. Don't add a preposition to necesitar.

title: importar vs interesar

triggers.explanation: Doubt means you don't take the statement as fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudo que le importe.
examples.en: I doubt it matters to him.
examples.note: Importar works like gustar. Regular: importe.

examples.es: Dudo que les interesen las noticias.
examples.en: I doubt the news interests them.
examples.note: Las noticias is plural, so interesen.

examples.es: Dudo que me importe su opinión.
examples.en: I doubt his opinion matters to me.
examples.note: Importar = to matter.

contrast.es: No dudo que me importa su opinión.
contrast.en: I don't doubt his opinion matters to me.
contrast.note: Dudar takes the subjunctive. No dudar expresses certainty, so the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Finding something strange is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es extraño que no te interese.
examples.en: It's strange that you aren't interested.
examples.note: Interesar works like gustar.

examples.es: Es extraño que no te importen los precios.
examples.en: It's strange that prices don't matter to you.
examples.note: Los precios is plural, so importen.

examples.es: Es extraño que no le interese el fútbol.
examples.en: It's strange that he isn't interested in football.
examples.note: Interesar = to interest.

contrast.es: Es cierto que no le interesa el fútbol.
contrast.en: It's true that he isn't interested in football.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es extraño reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something not established as true.

examples.es: Aunque no te interese, escucha.
examples.en: Even if it doesn't interest you, listen.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Aunque no te importe, avísame.
examples.en: Even if you don't mind, let me know.
examples.note: No importar = to not mind.

examples.es: Aunque le importe poco, se lo diré.
examples.en: Even if he cares little, I'll tell him.
examples.note: Importar poco = to matter little.

contrast.es: Aunque le importa poco, se lo diré.
contrast.en: Although he cares little, I'll tell him.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Importar and interesar both work like gustar, so the thing that matters is the subject and agrees: 'que te importe el precio', 'que te importen los precios'. Both are regular (importe, interese). 'No me importa que' + subjunctive means 'I don't mind that'.

title: funcionar vs trabajar

triggers.explanation: Finding something odd is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es raro que el coche no funcione.
examples.en: It's odd that the car doesn't work.
examples.note: Funcionar = for machines to work.

examples.es: Es raro que trabajes los domingos.
examples.en: It's odd that you work on Sundays.
examples.note: Trabajar = for people to work.

examples.es: Es raro que trabaje de noche.
examples.en: It's odd that he works at night.
examples.note: Trabajar de noche = to work nights.

contrast.es: Es cierto que trabaja de noche.
contrast.en: It's true that he works at night.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es raro judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá funcione el plan.
examples.en: I hope the plan works.
examples.note: Funcionar also applies to plans and ideas.

examples.es: Ojalá funcionen los frenos.
examples.en: I hope the brakes work.
examples.note: Los frenos is plural, so funcionen.

examples.es: Ojalá funcione el wifi en el hotel.
examples.en: I hope the wifi works at the hotel.
examples.note: A hope, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: El wifi funciona en el hotel.
contrast.en: The wifi works at the hotel.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A hope uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Revisa el motor para que funcione.
examples.en: Check the engine so that it works.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Trabajo duro para que funcione el negocio.
examples.en: I work hard so that the business works.
examples.note: Trabajar for the person, funcionar for the business.

examples.es: Llama al técnico para que funcione la lavadora.
examples.en: Call the technician so that the washing machine works.
examples.note: A purpose with a different subject.

contrast.es: Llamo al técnico porque no funciona la lavadora.
contrast.en: I'm calling the technician because the washing machine isn't working.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Funcionar is for machines, systems and plans, and trabajar is for people. Both are regular (funcione, trabaje), so the catch is choosing the right one: 'que el coche funcione', never 'que el coche trabaje'. Trabajar de means to work as: 'que trabajes de camarero'.

title: cumplir

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando cumplas dieciocho, podrás conducir.
examples.en: When you turn eighteen, you'll be able to drive.
examples.note: Cumplir años = to turn a given age.

examples.es: Cuando cumpla treinta años, haré una fiesta.
examples.en: When I turn thirty, I'll have a party.
examples.note: Cumplir + number = to turn that age.

examples.es: Cuando cumpla con mis obligaciones, descansaré.
examples.en: When I've fulfilled my obligations, I'll rest.
examples.note: Cumplir con = to fulfil a duty.

contrast.es: Cuando cumplo con mis obligaciones, descanso.
contrast.en: Whenever I've fulfilled my obligations, I rest.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Demanding something is trying to influence, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te exijo que cumplas las normas.
examples.en: I demand that you follow the rules.
examples.note: Cumplir las normas = to follow the rules.

examples.es: Te exijo que cumplas con el plazo.
examples.en: I demand that you meet the deadline.
examples.note: Cumplir con el plazo = to meet a deadline.

examples.es: Te exijo que cumplas lo prometido.
examples.en: I demand that you do what you promised.
examples.note: Cumplir lo prometido = to keep a promise.

contrast.es: Sé que cumples lo prometido.
contrast.en: I know you do what you promised.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Exigir expresses a demand (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Judging something unfair is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No es justo que no cumplan su palabra.
examples.en: It's not fair that they don't keep their word.
examples.note: Cumplir la palabra = to keep your word.

examples.es: No es justo que cumpla la condena sin pruebas.
examples.en: It's not fair that he serves the sentence without evidence.
examples.note: Cumplir una condena = to serve a sentence.

examples.es: No es justo que cumpla todo el castigo.
examples.en: It's not fair that he serves the whole punishment.
examples.note: A judgement about fairness.

contrast.es: Es cierto que cumple todo el castigo.
contrast.en: It's true that he serves the whole punishment.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). No es justo judges it (subjunctive).

tricky: Cumplir is regular (cumpla, cumplas, cumplan) but its meaning depends on the object: 'que cumplas veinte años' (turn twenty), 'que cumplas con tu deber' (fulfil it, with con), 'que cumplas tu promesa' (keep it, no preposition). Learners often drop the con after 'cumplir con'.

title: llegar vs alcanzar

triggers.explanation: Saying something is impossible denies it as a fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es imposible que lleguemos a tiempo.
examples.en: It's impossible that we'll arrive on time.
examples.note: Llegar needs gu before e: lleguemos.

examples.es: Es imposible que alcance el estante.
examples.en: It's impossible for me to reach the shelf.
examples.note: Alcanzar needs z→c: alcance.

examples.es: Es imposible que alcancemos el objetivo.
examples.en: It's impossible that we'll reach the target.
examples.note: Alcanzar un objetivo = to reach a goal.

contrast.es: Es cierto que alcanzamos el objetivo.
contrast.en: It's true that we reach the target.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es imposible denies it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando llegues, llámame.
examples.en: When you arrive, call me.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando alcances la cima, mira abajo.
examples.en: When you reach the summit, look down.
examples.note: Alcanzar la cima = to reach the top.

examples.es: Cuando llegue el momento, lo sabrás.
examples.en: When the moment comes, you'll know.
examples.note: A future moment, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando llega el momento, siempre se sabe.
contrast.en: When the moment comes, you always know.
contrast.note: A general truth uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te subo a la silla para que alcances el estante.
examples.en: I'll lift you onto the chair so that you can reach the shelf.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Te despierto temprano para que llegues a tiempo.
examples.en: I'll wake you early so that you arrive on time.
examples.note: Llegar a tiempo = to arrive on time.

examples.es: Ahorra para que te alcance el dinero.
examples.en: Save so that you have enough money.
examples.note: Alcanzar also means to be enough (te alcanza el dinero), especially in Latin America.

contrast.es: Con lo que ahorras, te alcanza el dinero.
contrast.en: With what you save, you have enough money.
contrast.note: A fact uses the indicative. A purpose uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Llegar needs g→gu before e: llegue, llegues, lleguemos. Alcanzar needs z→c: alcance, alcances, alcancemos, never 'alcanze'. Alcanzar also means to be enough (especially in Latin America): 'que te alcance el dinero'. Llegar goes with a + place, alcanzar takes a direct object.

title: quitar vs quitarse

triggers.explanation: Saying what would be better is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es mejor que te quites los zapatos.
examples.en: It's better if you take your shoes off.
examples.note: Quitarse = to take off your own clothes.

examples.es: Es mejor que quitemos esto de aquí.
examples.en: It's better if we remove this from here.
examples.note: Quitar = to remove something.

examples.es: Es mejor que le quites los zapatos al niño.
examples.en: It's better if you take the child's shoes off.
examples.note: Quitar + le = take something off someone else.

contrast.es: Es obvio que le quitas los zapatos al niño.
contrast.en: It's obvious you take the child's shoes off.
contrast.note: Es obvio states a fact (indicative). Es mejor gives advice (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te quites el abrigo, cuélgalo.
examples.en: When you take off your coat, hang it up.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando quites los platos, pasa la fregona.
examples.en: When you clear the plates, mop the floor.
examples.note: Quitar los platos = to clear the table.

examples.es: Cuando se quite las gafas, verás sus ojos.
examples.en: When he takes his glasses off, you'll see his eyes.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando se quita las gafas, se le ven los ojos.
contrast.en: Whenever he takes his glasses off, you can see his eyes.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ponle hielo para que se le quite el dolor.
examples.en: Put ice on it so the pain goes away.
examples.note: Quitársele algo a alguien = for something to go away.

examples.es: Usa vinagre para que se quite la mancha.
examples.en: Use vinegar so that the stain comes out.
examples.note: Se quite = the stain comes out.

examples.es: Llámalos para que me quiten la multa.
examples.en: Call them so that they cancel my fine.
examples.note: Quitar la multa = to cancel a fine.

contrast.es: Llámalos para quitarte la multa.
contrast.en: Call them to get rid of your fine.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Quitar is regular (quite, quites, quitemos), with no spelling change. The reflexive changes who is affected: 'que quites los zapatos' (take someone else's off) vs 'que te quites los zapatos' (take your own off). 'Que se te quite el dolor' means that the pain goes away.

title: llevar vs vestirse (wear)

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quiero que lleves tu abrigo.
examples.en: I want you to wear your coat.
examples.note: Llevar = to wear (be wearing).

examples.es: Quiero que te vistas rápido.
examples.en: I want you to get dressed quickly.
examples.note: Vestirse has e→i: vistas, never 'vestas'.

examples.es: Quiero que lleves el vestido azul.
examples.en: I want you to wear the blue dress.
examples.note: Llevar = what you have on.

contrast.es: Sé que llevas el vestido azul.
contrast.en: I know you're wearing the blue dress.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Querer expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te vistas, avísame.
examples.en: When you get dressed, let me know.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando nos vistamos, saldremos.
examples.en: When we've got dressed, we'll go out.
examples.note: Nosotros also has e→i: vistamos.

examples.es: Cuando lleves traje, nadie te reconocerá.
examples.en: When you wear a suit, nobody will recognise you.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando llevas traje, nadie te reconoce.
contrast.en: Whenever you wear a suit, nobody recognises you.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Prepara la ropa para que se vista rápido.
examples.en: Get the clothes ready so that he gets dressed quickly.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Dale un abrigo para que lleve algo caliente.
examples.en: Give him a coat so that he wears something warm.
examples.note: Llevar algo caliente = to have something warm on.

examples.es: Dale un pañuelo para que lleve la cabeza cubierta.
examples.en: Give her a scarf so that she keeps her head covered.
examples.note: A purpose with a different subject.

contrast.es: Lleva la cabeza cubierta porque hace frío.
contrast.en: She keeps her head covered because it's cold.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Vestirse changes e→i in every form: me vista, te vistas, se vistan, nos vistamos. Llevar is regular (lleve). Llevar is to be wearing, vestirse is to get dressed, and ponerse is to put on: 'que lleves corbata' vs 'que te vistas'. Vestirse de + colour or costume means to dress as.

title: ganar vs ganarse

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá gane mi equipo.
examples.en: I hope my team wins.
examples.note: Ganar = to win.

examples.es: Ojalá ganemos el partido.
examples.en: I hope we win the match.
examples.note: Nosotros form: ganemos.

examples.es: Ojalá ganen más dinero este año.
examples.en: I hope they earn more money this year.
examples.note: Ganar dinero = to earn money.

contrast.es: Ganan más dinero este año.
contrast.en: They earn more money this year.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A hope uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando gane dinero, viajaré.
examples.en: When I earn money, I'll travel.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te ganes la vida, entenderás.
examples.en: When you earn your own living, you'll understand.
examples.note: Ganarse la vida = to earn a living. Reflexive.

examples.es: Cuando se gane tu confianza, hablará.
examples.en: When he's earned your trust, he'll talk.
examples.note: Ganarse la confianza = to earn trust.

contrast.es: Cuando se gana tu confianza, habla.
contrast.en: When he earns your trust, he talks.
contrast.note: A general truth uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Entrénalo para que gane la carrera.
examples.en: Train him so that he wins the race.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Dale una oportunidad para que se gane el respeto.
examples.en: Give him a chance so that he earns respect.
examples.note: Ganarse el respeto = to earn respect. Different subjects.

examples.es: Ayúdale para que se gane la vida con dignidad.
examples.en: Help him so that he earns a living with dignity.
examples.note: Ganarse la vida, always with the reflexive.

contrast.es: Se gana la vida con dignidad.
contrast.en: He earns a living with dignity.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A purpose uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Ganar and ganarse are both regular (gane, ganes). Always say 'ganarse la vida' with the reflexive, never 'ganar la vida'. Ganar is to win or earn, and ganarse is to earn something through your own effort: 'que te ganes el respeto'. 'Ganar a alguien' means to beat them.

title: soñar

triggers.explanation: Wishing something for someone is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te deseo que sueñes cosas bonitas.
examples.en: I hope you dream of nice things.
examples.note: Soñar has o→ue: sueñes.

examples.es: Te deseo que sueñes con una vida mejor.
examples.en: I hope you dream of a better life.
examples.note: Soñar con = to dream of. Always con.

examples.es: Te deseo que sueñes en grande.
examples.en: I hope you dream big.
examples.note: Soñar en grande = to aim high (aspire).

contrast.es: Sueñas en grande.
contrast.en: You dream big.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A wish uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Saying something isn't odd is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No es raro que sueñes con ella.
examples.en: It's not odd that you dream about her.
examples.note: Soñar con, never 'soñar de' or 'sobre'.

examples.es: No es raro que sueñen con viajar.
examples.en: It's not odd that they dream of travelling.
examples.note: Soñar con + infinitive = to dream of doing.

examples.es: No es raro que sueñe con su infancia.
examples.en: It's not odd that he dreams about his childhood.
examples.note: Soñar con = to dream about.

contrast.es: Es cierto que sueña con su infancia.
contrast.en: It's true that he dreams about his childhood.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). No es raro judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando sueñes con él, cuéntamelo.
examples.en: When you dream about him, tell me.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando soñemos juntos, todo será posible.
examples.en: When we dream together, everything will be possible.
examples.note: Nosotros keeps the o: soñemos.

examples.es: Cuando sueñe con volar, me despertaré feliz.
examples.en: When I dream of flying, I'll wake up happy.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando sueño con volar, me despierto feliz.
contrast.en: Whenever I dream of flying, I wake up happy.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Soñar always takes con ('que sueñes con ella'), never 'de' or 'sobre'. It has an o→ue stem change: sueñe, sueñes, sueñen, but soñemos in nosotros. It covers both dreaming asleep and dreaming of a goal.

title: olvidar vs olvidarse

triggers.explanation: Not wanting something to happen is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No quiero que olvides mi cumpleaños.
examples.en: I don't want you to forget my birthday.
examples.note: Olvidar + object = to forget.

examples.es: No quiero que te olvides de las llaves.
examples.en: I don't want you to forget the keys.
examples.note: Olvidarse de = to forget about. Reflexive with de.

examples.es: No quiero que olvides las llaves en el coche.
examples.en: I don't want you to leave the keys in the car.
examples.note: Olvidar can mean to leave something behind.

contrast.es: Veo que olvidas las llaves en el coche.
contrast.en: I see you leave the keys in the car.
contrast.note: Veo que states a fact (indicative). Querer expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Saying something is easy to happen is a judgement of likelihood, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es fácil que olvides el paraguas.
examples.en: You could easily forget the umbrella.
examples.note: Es fácil que = it's likely that.

examples.es: Es fácil que nos olvidemos de todo.
examples.en: We could easily forget everything.
examples.note: Olvidarse de todo = to forget everything.

examples.es: Es fácil que se olvide de avisarte.
examples.en: He could easily forget to tell you.
examples.note: Olvidarse de + infinitive = to forget to.

contrast.es: Es evidente que se olvida de avisarte.
contrast.en: It's obvious he forgets to tell you.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es fácil que judges likelihood (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hasn't happened yet.

examples.es: Apúntalo antes de que se te olvide.
examples.en: Write it down before you forget it.
examples.note: Se te olvide = it slips your mind.

examples.es: Dímelo antes de que me olvide.
examples.en: Tell me before I forget.
examples.note: Me olvide: I forget.

examples.es: Llámala antes de que se olvide de nosotros.
examples.en: Call her before she forgets about us.
examples.note: The forgetting hasn't happened yet.

contrast.es: La llamé después de que se olvidó de nosotros.
contrast.en: I called her after she forgot about us.
contrast.note: Después de que with a completed past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Olvidar and olvidarse are both regular (olvide, olvides, olvidemos). 'Olvidar' + object is the plain verb, 'olvidarse de' is the reflexive version, and 'se me olvidó' is the accidental one: 'antes de que se te olvide'. Olvidar las llaves can also mean leaving them behind.

title: notar vs fijarse

triggers.explanation: Calling something important is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es importante que notes la diferencia.
examples.en: It's important that you notice the difference.
examples.note: Notar = to notice, passively. Regular: notes.

examples.es: Es importante que te fijes en los detalles.
examples.en: It's important that you pay attention to the details.
examples.note: Fijarse en = to pay attention to. Always en.

examples.es: Es importante que te fijes bien en la señal.
examples.en: It's important that you look carefully at the sign.
examples.note: Fijarse bien = to pay close attention.

contrast.es: Es obvio que te fijas bien en la señal.
contrast.en: It's obvious you look carefully at the sign.
contrast.note: Es obvio states a fact (indicative). Es importante judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que note el cambio.
examples.en: I don't think he'll notice the change.
examples.note: Notar el cambio = to notice a change.

examples.es: No creo que se fije en nada.
examples.en: I don't think she pays attention to anything.
examples.note: Fijarse en nada = to take notice of nothing.

examples.es: No creo que se fije en lo que digo.
examples.en: I don't think he pays attention to what I say.
examples.note: Fijarse en = to focus on.

contrast.es: Creo que se fija en lo que digo.
contrast.en: I think he pays attention to what I say.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Habla más alto para que lo noten.
examples.en: Speak louder so that they notice.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Pon un cartel para que se fijen en la oferta.
examples.en: Put up a sign so that they pay attention to the offer.
examples.note: Fijarse en = to focus on.

examples.es: Cambia el color para que se note menos.
examples.en: Change the colour so that it shows less.
examples.note: Notarse = to show, to be noticeable.

contrast.es: Cambio el color porque se nota mucho.
contrast.en: I'm changing the colour because it shows a lot.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Notar is regular (note), and fijarse is regular too (me fije, te fijes, nos fijemos) but always needs en: 'que te fijes en esto'. Notar is passive noticing and fijarse is deliberate attention. 'Que se note' means for it to show.

title: preocupar vs preocuparse

triggers.explanation: Saying something makes no sense is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No tiene sentido que te preocupes.
examples.en: There's no point in you worrying.
examples.note: Preocuparse = to worry. Reflexive: te preocupes.

examples.es: No tiene sentido que me preocupe tanto.
examples.en: There's no point in my worrying so much.
examples.note: Me preocupe: I worry.

examples.es: No tiene sentido que te preocupes por eso.
examples.en: There's no point in you worrying about that.
examples.note: Preocuparse por = to worry about.

contrast.es: Siempre te preocupas por eso.
contrast.en: You always worry about that.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A judgement uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que le preocupe.
examples.en: I don't think it worries him.
examples.note: Preocupar works like gustar: the thing worries the person.

examples.es: No creo que les preocupen los gastos.
examples.en: I don't think the costs worry them.
examples.note: Los gastos is plural, so preocupen.

examples.es: No creo que se preocupe por nada.
examples.en: I don't think he worries about anything.
examples.note: Preocuparse por nada = to worry about nothing.

contrast.es: Creo que se preocupa por todo.
contrast.en: I think he worries about everything.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Llámame para que no me preocupe.
examples.en: Call me so that I don't worry.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Avísame para que no se preocupen tus padres.
examples.en: Let me know so that your parents don't worry.
examples.note: Plural subject: tus padres.

examples.es: Escríbele para que no se preocupe.
examples.en: Write to her so that she doesn't worry.
examples.note: Purpose with a different subject.

contrast.es: Le escribo porque se preocupa.
contrast.en: I'm writing to her because she worries.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Preocupar works like gustar and agrees with the thing that worries: 'que te preocupe el dinero', 'que te preocupen los gastos'. Preocuparse is reflexive with por or de: 'que te preocupes por él'. Both are regular, and 'no te preocupes' is itself a subjunctive form used as a command.

title: resultar

triggers.explanation: Likelihood isn't certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es probable que resulte caro.
examples.en: It will probably turn out expensive.
examples.note: Resultar + adjective = to turn out to be.

examples.es: Es probable que resulten útiles.
examples.en: They will probably turn out useful.
examples.note: Plural subject, so resulten.

examples.es: Es probable que resulte que tienes razón.
examples.en: It will probably turn out that you're right.
examples.note: Resultar que = it turns out that.

contrast.es: Resulta que tienes razón.
contrast.en: It turns out you're right.
contrast.note: Resulta que states the outcome as a fact (indicative).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something not established as true.

examples.es: Aunque resulte difícil, lo haré.
examples.en: Even if it turns out hard, I'll do it.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Aunque resulte raro, es verdad.
examples.en: Strange as it may seem, it's true.
examples.note: Resultar raro = to seem strange.

examples.es: Aunque me resulte difícil entenderlo, lo intentaré.
examples.en: Even if I find it hard to understand, I'll try.
examples.note: Me resulte works like gustar: it turns out hard for me.

contrast.es: Aunque me resulta difícil entenderlo, lo intento.
contrast.en: Although I find it hard to understand, I'm trying.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando resulte necesario, avisaremos.
examples.en: When it becomes necessary, we'll let you know.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando resulte más barato, compraremos.
examples.en: When it becomes cheaper, we'll buy.
examples.note: Resultar más barato = to turn out cheaper.

examples.es: Cuando resulte evidente, todos lo verán.
examples.en: When it becomes obvious, everyone will see it.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando resulta evidente, todos lo ven.
contrast.en: When it becomes obvious, everyone sees it.
contrast.note: A general truth uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Resultar is regular (resulte, resulten) but flexible: turn out to be ('que resulte útil'), gustar-style ('me resulte difícil') or 'resulta que' (it turns out that, indicative). It's often a more elegant stand-in for ser: 'resulte caro' rather than 'sea caro'.

title: sobrar vs bastar

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá sobre comida.
examples.en: I hope there's food left over.
examples.note: Sobrar = to be left over, to be too much.

examples.es: Ojalá nos basten los ahorros.
examples.en: I hope our savings are enough.
examples.note: Los ahorros is plural, so basten.

examples.es: Ojalá baste con una llamada.
examples.en: I hope a phone call is enough.
examples.note: Bastar con = to be enough.

contrast.es: Basta con una llamada.
contrast.en: A phone call is enough.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A hope uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: A possibility isn't a fact, so the subjunctive is needed.

examples.es: Es posible que sobre comida.
examples.en: It's possible there'll be food left over.
examples.note: Sobrar works like gustar: the food is the subject.

examples.es: Es posible que nos sobren entradas.
examples.en: It's possible we'll have spare tickets.
examples.note: Entradas is plural, so sobren.

examples.es: Es posible que con esto baste.
examples.en: It's possible that this will be enough.
examples.note: Bastar = to be enough.

contrast.es: Seguro que con esto basta.
contrast.en: This is sure to be enough.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Es posible que = possibility (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando sobre tiempo, descansa.
examples.en: When you have time to spare, rest.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando baste con una firma, avísame.
examples.en: When a signature is enough, let me know.
examples.note: Bastar con = to be enough.

examples.es: Cuando te sobre dinero, ahorra.
examples.en: When you have money left over, save it.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando te sobra dinero, ahorras.
contrast.en: Whenever you have money left over, you save it.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Sobrar and bastar both work like gustar and agree with the thing: 'que te sobre tiempo', 'que te sobren euros', 'que baste con eso'. The subjunctives are regular: sobre, sobren, baste, basten. 'Basta de' also means 'enough of' (stop it).

title: costar vs valer

triggers.explanation: Doubt means you don't take the statement as fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudo que cueste tanto.
examples.en: I doubt it costs that much.
examples.note: Costar has o→ue: cueste.

examples.es: Dudo que valga la pena.
examples.en: I doubt it's worth it.
examples.note: Valer is irregular: valga, with -g-.

examples.es: Dudo que valgan tanto estos cuadros.
examples.en: I doubt these paintings are worth that much.
examples.note: Valer = to be worth. Plural: valgan.

contrast.es: No dudo que valen tanto estos cuadros.
contrast.en: I don't doubt these paintings are worth that much.
contrast.note: Dudar takes the subjunctive. No dudar expresses certainty, so the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + subjunctive means 'even if', for something not established as true.

examples.es: Aunque cueste caro, lo compro.
examples.en: Even if it costs a lot, I'll buy it.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Aunque valga poco, me gusta.
examples.en: Even if it's worth little, I like it.
examples.note: Valer poco = to be worth little.

examples.es: Aunque cueste más, vale la pena.
examples.en: Even if it costs more, it's worth it.
examples.note: Hypothetical price.

contrast.es: Aunque cuesta más, vale la pena.
contrast.en: Although it costs more, it's worth it.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando cueste menos, lo compraremos.
examples.en: When it costs less, we'll buy it.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando valga la pena, lo haré.
examples.en: When it's worth it, I'll do it.
examples.note: Valer la pena = to be worth it.

examples.es: Cuando cueste más de cien euros, pídeme permiso.
examples.en: When it costs more than a hundred euros, ask me for permission.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando cuesta más de cien euros, me pides permiso.
contrast.en: Whenever it costs more than a hundred euros, you ask me for permission.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Costar has o→ue (cueste, cuesten) but costemos in nosotros, and valer is irregular: valga, valgas, valgamos, valgan, with the -g- of valgo. 'Que valga la pena' means worth it. Costar is what you pay and valer is what it's worth.

title: durar vs tardar

triggers.explanation: Likelihood isn't certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es probable que dure poco.
examples.en: It probably won't last long.
examples.note: Durar = how long something lasts.

examples.es: Es probable que tardes una hora.
examples.en: It will probably take you an hour.
examples.note: Tardar = how long something takes you.

examples.es: Es probable que la reunión dure dos horas.
examples.en: It's likely the meeting will last two hours.
examples.note: Durar = the length of an event.

contrast.es: Seguro que la reunión dura dos horas.
contrast.en: The meeting is sure to last two hours.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Es probable que = likelihood (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuídalo para que dure.
examples.en: Look after it so that it lasts.
examples.note: Durar = to last, to be durable.

examples.es: Te llevo en coche para que no tardes.
examples.en: I'll drive you so that you don't take long.
examples.note: No tardar = not to take long. Different subjects.

examples.es: Sal pronto para que no tardemos en llegar.
examples.en: Leave soon so that we don't take long to get there.
examples.note: Tardar en + infinitive = to take a while to.

contrast.es: Salgo pronto para no tardar en llegar.
contrast.en: I'm leaving soon so as not to take long to get there.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando tardes en llegar, llámame.
examples.en: Whenever you're going to take a while to arrive, call me.
examples.note: Tardar en = to take time to.

examples.es: Cuando dure demasiado, nos vamos.
examples.en: When it goes on too long, we'll leave.
examples.note: Durar demasiado = to go on too long.

examples.es: Cuando tarde más de una hora, avisaré.
examples.en: When I take more than an hour, I'll let you know.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando tarda más de una hora, avisa.
contrast.en: Whenever he takes more than an hour, he lets you know.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Durar is how long something lasts (dure) and tardar is how long it takes (tarde). 'Que tardes una hora' (it takes you an hour) is not 'que dure una hora' (it lasts an hour). Tardar en + infinitive means to take a while to. Both verbs are regular.

title: pagar vs cobrar

triggers.explanation: Calling something reasonable is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es razonable que pagues tu parte.
examples.en: It's reasonable that you pay your share.
examples.note: Pagar needs gu before e: pagues.

examples.es: Es razonable que cobren por el servicio.
examples.en: It's reasonable that they charge for the service.
examples.note: Cobrar por = to charge for.

examples.es: Es razonable que cobre más por las horas extra.
examples.en: It's reasonable that she gets paid more for overtime.
examples.note: Cobrar = to receive pay.

contrast.es: Es evidente que cobra más por las horas extra.
contrast.en: It's obvious she gets paid more for overtime.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es razonable judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Hasta que about something not yet completed takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: No salgas hasta que pagues.
examples.en: Don't leave until you've paid.
examples.note: Future / unfinished event.

examples.es: No me voy hasta que me cobren.
examples.en: I'm not leaving until they charge me.
examples.note: Cobrar a alguien = to charge someone.

examples.es: No me voy hasta que cobre lo que me deben.
examples.en: I'm not leaving until I collect what they owe me.
examples.note: Cobrar = to collect money owed.

contrast.es: No me fui hasta que cobré lo que me debían.
contrast.en: I didn't leave until I collected what they owed me.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dame efectivo para que pague.
examples.en: Give me cash so that I can pay.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Te contrato para que cobres a final de mes.
examples.en: I'm hiring you so that you get paid at the end of the month.
examples.note: Cobrar a final de mes = to get paid at month end.

examples.es: Envía la factura para que nos paguen.
examples.en: Send the invoice so that they pay us.
examples.note: Pagar needs gu: paguen.

contrast.es: Envío la factura porque nos deben dinero.
contrast.en: I'm sending the invoice because they owe us money.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Pagar needs g→gu before e: pague, pagues, paguemos, never 'page'. Cobrar is regular (cobre). Pagar is handing money over, and cobrar is receiving it, or charging it: 'que pagues' (you give) vs 'que cobres' (you receive or charge). 'Pagar por' something, 'pagar a' someone.

title: mandar vs enviar

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quiero que me mandes una foto.
examples.en: I want you to send me a photo.
examples.note: Mandar = to send (casual).

examples.es: Quiero que envíes el paquete hoy.
examples.en: I want you to send the package today.
examples.note: Enviar keeps an accent in envíes, envíe and envíen.

examples.es: Quiero que mandes a tu hermano a la tienda.
examples.en: I want you to send your brother to the shop.
examples.note: Mandar a alguien a + place = to send someone.

contrast.es: Sé que mandas a tu hermano a la tienda.
contrast.en: I know you send your brother to the shop.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Querer expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto mande el correo, te aviso.
examples.en: As soon as I send the email, I'll let you know.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: En cuanto envíes el archivo, lo reviso.
examples.en: As soon as you send the file, I'll check it.
examples.note: Enviar is a touch more formal.

examples.es: En cuanto manden el paquete, te llamo.
examples.en: As soon as they send the parcel, I'll call you.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: En cuanto mandaron el paquete, te llamé.
contrast.en: As soon as they sent the parcel, I called you.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dame tu dirección para que te envíe el libro.
examples.en: Give me your address so that I can send you the book.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Dame tu número para que te mande un mensaje.
examples.en: Give me your number so that I can send you a message.
examples.note: Mandar un mensaje = to send a message.

examples.es: Escríbeles para que nos manden el presupuesto.
examples.en: Write to them so that they send us the quote.
examples.note: Different subjects.

contrast.es: Les escribo para mandarles el presupuesto.
contrast.en: I'm writing to them to send them the quote.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Enviar keeps an accent in envíe, envíes, envíen (but enviemos has none), while mandar is regular (mande). Enviar is neutral and a touch formal, and mandar is more casual, and it also means to order: 'que mande él' can mean that he gives the orders. 'Mandar a alguien a paseo' means telling them to get lost.

title: casarse

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá te cases pronto.
examples.en: I hope you get married soon.
examples.note: Casarse = to get married. Regular: te cases.

examples.es: Ojalá se casen en primavera.
examples.en: I hope they get married in the spring.
examples.note: Ellos form: se casen.

examples.es: Ojalá se case con alguien que la quiera.
examples.en: I hope she marries someone who loves her.
examples.note: Casarse con = to marry. Always con.

contrast.es: Se casa con alguien que la quiere.
contrast.en: She's marrying someone who loves her.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A hope uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hasn't happened yet.

examples.es: Hablemos antes de que te cases.
examples.en: Let's talk before you get married.
examples.note: Different subjects, so antes de que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Ahorra antes de que se casen.
examples.en: Save before they get married.
examples.note: The wedding hasn't happened yet.

examples.es: Habla con ella antes de que se case con él.
examples.en: Talk to her before she marries him.
examples.note: Casarse con él, never 'casarse a él'.

contrast.es: Hablé con ella después de que se casó con él.
contrast.en: I talked to her after she married him.
contrast.note: Después de que with a completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te cases, invítame.
examples.en: When you get married, invite me.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando se casen, vivirán aquí.
examples.en: When they get married, they'll live here.
examples.note: Future event.

examples.es: Cuando me case con ella, cambiaré.
examples.en: When I marry her, I'll change.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando alguien se casa, cambia su vida.
contrast.en: When someone gets married, their life changes.
contrast.note: A general truth uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Casarse is regular (me case, te cases, nos casemos) but always takes con: 'que te cases con ella', never 'casarse a'. Don't mix the verb with the state: casarse is the act, estar casado is being married. Casar (non-reflexive) means to marry someone off or to officiate.

title: despedir vs despedirse

triggers.explanation: Calling something unfair is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es injusto que te despidan.
examples.en: It's unfair that they fire you.
examples.note: Despedir = to fire. E→i stem: despidan.

examples.es: Es injusto que despidan a tantos trabajadores.
examples.en: It's unfair that they fire so many workers.
examples.note: Despedir a = to fire someone.

examples.es: Es injusto que lo despidan sin avisar.
examples.en: It's unfair that they fire him without warning.
examples.note: Despedir sin avisar = to fire without notice.

contrast.es: Es cierto que lo despiden sin avisar.
contrast.en: It's true that they fire him without warning.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es injusto reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hasn't happened yet.

examples.es: Avísale antes de que lo despidan.
examples.en: Warn him before they fire him.
examples.note: Different subjects, so antes de que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Llega antes de que se despida el presidente.
examples.en: Arrive before the president says goodbye.
examples.note: Despedirse = to say goodbye.

examples.es: Hablemos antes de que me despidan.
examples.en: Let's talk before they fire me.
examples.note: The firing hasn't happened yet.

contrast.es: Hablamos después de que me despidieron.
contrast.en: We spoke after they fired me.
contrast.note: Después de que with a completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te despidas, abraza a todos.
examples.en: When you say goodbye, hug everyone.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando despidan al jefe, habrá cambios.
examples.en: When they fire the boss, there'll be changes.
examples.note: Future event.

examples.es: Cuando se despida, no llores.
examples.en: When she says goodbye, don't cry.
examples.note: A future moment, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando se despide, siempre llora.
contrast.en: Whenever she says goodbye, she always cries.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Despedir and despedirse change e→i in every form: despida, despidas, despidamos, despidan. Despedir is to fire (or see someone off) and despedirse is to say goodbye (despedirse de): 'que te despidas de ellos' versus 'que te despidan' is a big difference for one letter.

title: morir vs matar

triggers.explanation: Fear is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Tengo miedo de que se muera la planta.
examples.en: I'm afraid the plant will die.
examples.note: Morirse has o→ue: muera.

examples.es: Tengo miedo de que maten al protagonista en la serie.
examples.en: I'm afraid they'll kill off the main character in the series.
examples.note: Matar is regular: maten.

examples.es: Tengo miedo de que muera sin verme.
examples.en: I'm afraid he'll die without seeing me.
examples.note: Morir is the neutral verb for dying.

contrast.es: Sé que muere sin verme.
contrast.en: I know he dies without seeing me.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Tener miedo de que expresses fear (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hasn't happened yet.

examples.es: Riega la planta antes de que se muera.
examples.en: Water the plant before it dies.
examples.note: Different subjects, so antes de que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Carga el móvil antes de que se muera la batería.
examples.en: Charge your phone before the battery dies.
examples.note: Morirse is used for batteries and plants too.

examples.es: Come algo antes de que nos muramos de hambre.
examples.en: Eat something before we die of hunger.
examples.note: Nosotros shows o→u: muramos.

contrast.es: Comimos algo después de que casi nos morimos de hambre.
contrast.en: We ate something after we almost died of hunger.
contrast.note: Después de que with a completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Quizás expresses doubt, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quizás me muera de risa.
examples.en: Maybe I'll die laughing.
examples.note: Morirse de risa = to die laughing.

examples.es: Quizás mate el tiempo leyendo.
examples.en: Maybe I'll kill time reading.
examples.note: Matar el tiempo = to kill time.

examples.es: Quizás mate dos pájaros de un tiro.
examples.en: Maybe I'll kill two birds with one stone.
examples.note: A fixed expression.

contrast.es: Seguro que mato dos pájaros de un tiro.
contrast.en: I'm sure I'll kill two birds with one stone.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Quizás = doubt (subjunctive).

tricky: Morir has o→ue (muera, mueran) and o→u in nosotros (muramos). Matar is regular (mate). In everyday talk morirse is more common than morir, and matarse means to kill yourself or to get killed. Watch the idioms: morirse de hambre or de risa, matar el tiempo.

title: oler vs saber a

triggers.explanation: Finding something odd is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es raro que huela tan bien.
examples.en: It's odd that it smells so good.
examples.note: Oler adds h- and o→ue: huela.

examples.es: Es raro que sepa a fresa.
examples.en: It's odd that it tastes of strawberry.
examples.note: Saber a = to taste of. Sepa is irregular.

examples.es: Es raro que huela a gas aquí.
examples.en: It's odd that it smells of gas here.
examples.note: Oler a = to smell of.

contrast.es: Es evidente que huele a gas aquí.
contrast.en: It's obvious it smells of gas here.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es raro reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Pon canela para que huela bien.
examples.en: Add cinnamon so that it smells good.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Añade limón para que sepa a fresco.
examples.en: Add lemon so that it tastes fresh.
examples.note: Saber a fresco = to taste fresh.

examples.es: Añade vainilla para que sepa a postre.
examples.en: Add vanilla so that it tastes like dessert.
examples.note: Saber a = to taste of. Never 'saber de' for taste.

contrast.es: Añado vainilla y sabe a postre.
contrast.en: I add vanilla and it tastes like dessert.
contrast.note: A fact uses the indicative. A purpose uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando huela a quemado, apaga el horno.
examples.en: When it smells of burning, turn off the oven.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando sepa a menta, ya estará listo.
examples.en: When it tastes of mint, it'll be ready.
examples.note: Saber a menta = to taste of mint.

examples.es: Cuando huela a lluvia, cierra las ventanas.
examples.en: When it smells of rain, close the windows.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando huele a lluvia, cierro las ventanas.
contrast.en: Whenever it smells of rain, I close the windows.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Oler takes h- and o→ue: huela, huelas, huelan, but olamos in nosotros (no h, no stem change). Saber a uses sepa a: 'que sepa a limón'. Oler a is smell of and saber a is taste of, so never 'sepa de' for taste ('saber de' means to know about).

title: cerrar vs apagar

triggers.explanation: Saying something is necessary is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es necesario que cierres la puerta.
examples.en: It's necessary that you close the door.
examples.note: Cerrar has e→ie: cierres.

examples.es: Es necesario que apagues el móvil.
examples.en: It's necessary that you turn off your phone.
examples.note: Apagar needs g→gu: apagues.

examples.es: Es necesario que cierres el gas.
examples.en: It's necessary that you turn off the gas.
examples.note: Cerrar el gas / el grifo = to turn off the gas or the tap.

contrast.es: Es evidente que cierras el gas.
contrast.en: It's obvious you turn off the gas.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es necesario judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando cierres, apaga las luces.
examples.en: When you close up, turn off the lights.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando apagues el ordenador, desenchúfalo.
examples.en: When you turn off the computer, unplug it.
examples.note: Apagar = to switch off a device or light.

examples.es: Cuando cierren la tienda, me iré.
examples.en: When they close the shop, I'll go.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando cierran la tienda, me voy.
contrast.en: Whenever they close the shop, I go.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Quizás expresses doubt, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quizás cierren hoy.
examples.en: Maybe they'll close today.
examples.note: Quizás + subjunctive = genuine doubt.

examples.es: Quizás apaguemos la calefacción.
examples.en: Maybe we'll turn off the heating.
examples.note: Nosotros: apaguemos, with gu.

examples.es: Quizás se apague el wifi por la noche.
examples.en: Maybe the wifi switches off at night.
examples.note: Apagarse = to switch off by itself.

contrast.es: Seguro que se apaga el wifi por la noche.
contrast.en: The wifi is sure to switch off at night.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Quizás = doubt (subjunctive).

tricky: Cerrar has e→ie (cierre, cierres, cierren) but cerremos in nosotros. Apagar needs g→gu: apague, apagues, apaguemos, never 'apage'. Standard Spanish uses 'apagar la luz', although cerrar la luz is heard in some Latin American regions, and cerrar is for taps, gas, doors and shops.

title: arreglar vs arreglarse

triggers.explanation: Needing someone else to act is a request, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Necesito que arregles el grifo.
examples.en: I need you to fix the tap.
examples.note: Arreglar = to fix.

examples.es: Necesito que te arregles rápido.
examples.en: I need you to get ready quickly.
examples.note: Arreglarse = to get ready.

examples.es: Necesito que me arregles el pelo.
examples.en: I need you to do my hair.
examples.note: Arreglar el pelo a alguien = to do someone's hair.

contrast.es: Necesito arreglarme el pelo.
contrast.en: I need to do my hair.
contrast.note: Same subject = infinitive. A different subject = que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Llama al técnico para que arregle la lavadora.
examples.en: Call the technician so that he fixes the washing machine.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Dale tiempo para que se arregle.
examples.en: Give her time so that she can get ready.
examples.note: Arreglarse = to freshen up.

examples.es: Ven temprano para que nos arreglemos juntos.
examples.en: Come early so that we get ready together.
examples.note: Nosotros reflexive: nos arreglemos.

contrast.es: Venimos temprano porque nos arreglamos juntos.
contrast.en: We come early because we get ready together.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando arregles el coche, avísame.
examples.en: When you've fixed the car, let me know.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando te arregles, saldremos.
examples.en: When you get ready, we'll go out.
examples.note: Arreglarse = to get ready.

examples.es: Cuando se arregle el problema, volveremos.
examples.en: When the problem gets sorted, we'll come back.
examples.note: Arreglarse also means to work out.

contrast.es: Cuando se arregla el problema, volvemos.
contrast.en: Whenever the problem gets sorted, we come back.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Arreglar and arreglarse are both regular (arregle, me arregle). The pronoun changes the meaning: 'que arregles el coche' (fix it) vs 'que te arregles' (get ready). 'Que se arregle' can also mean for it to get sorted, and 'arreglárselas' means to manage: 'que te las arregles'.

title: pegar

triggers.explanation: Calling something horrible is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es horrible que pegues a tu hermano.
examples.en: It's horrible that you hit your brother.
examples.note: Pegar a = to hit someone. G→gu: pegues.

examples.es: Es horrible que le peguen a un niño.
examples.en: It's horrible that they hit a child.
examples.note: Ellos form: peguen.

examples.es: Es horrible que le peguen a un animal indefenso.
examples.en: It's horrible that they hit a defenceless animal.
examples.note: Pegar = to hit.

contrast.es: Es cierto que le pegan a un animal indefenso.
contrast.en: It's true that they hit a defenceless animal.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es horrible reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Usa cola para que pegue bien.
examples.en: Use glue so that it sticks well.
examples.note: Pegar = to stick.

examples.es: Presiona un minuto para que se pegue.
examples.en: Press for a minute so that it sticks.
examples.note: Pegarse = to stick together.

examples.es: Elige otro color para que pegue con la camisa.
examples.en: Choose another colour so that it goes with the shirt.
examples.note: Pegar con = to match.

contrast.es: Elijo ese color porque pega con la camisa.
contrast.en: I choose that colour because it goes with the shirt.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando pegues el cartel, avísame.
examples.en: When you stick up the sign, let me know.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando le pegue un grito, vendrá.
examples.en: When I shout at him, he'll come.
examples.note: Pegar un grito = to let out a shout.

examples.es: Cuando pegue un portazo, sabré que está enfadado.
examples.en: When he slams the door, I'll know he's angry.
examples.note: Pegar un portazo = to slam the door.

contrast.es: Cuando pega un portazo, sé que está enfadado.
contrast.en: Whenever he slams the door, I know he's angry.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Pegar needs g→gu before e: pegue, pegues, peguemos, never 'pege'. It has three unrelated meanings (hit, stick, match) and lots of idioms: pegar un grito, pegar un portazo, pegar con. Use 'pegar a' for hitting a person.

title: meter vs poner

triggers.explanation: Preferring that someone else act in a certain way is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Prefiero que metas la ropa en la maleta.
examples.en: I prefer that you put the clothes in the suitcase.
examples.note: Meter en = to put inside.

examples.es: Prefiero que pongas el libro en la mesa.
examples.en: I prefer that you put the book on the table.
examples.note: Poner = to put on a surface. Poner has -g-: pongas.

examples.es: Prefiero que metas el coche en el garaje.
examples.en: I prefer that you put the car in the garage.
examples.note: Meter = to put inside something enclosed.

contrast.es: Sé que metes el coche en el garaje.
contrast.en: I know you put the car in the garage.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Preferir expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando metas la llave, gírala.
examples.en: When you put the key in, turn it.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando pongas la mesa, usa los platos buenos.
examples.en: When you set the table, use the good plates.
examples.note: Poner la mesa = to set the table.

examples.es: Cuando me meta en la cama, apaga la luz.
examples.en: When I get into bed, turn off the light.
examples.note: Meterse en = to get into.

contrast.es: Cuando me meto en la cama, apago la luz.
contrast.en: Whenever I get into bed, I turn off the light.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Abre la maleta para que meta la ropa.
examples.en: Open the suitcase so that I can put the clothes in.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Dame sitio para que ponga la bolsa.
examples.en: Make room so that I can put the bag down.
examples.note: Poner = to put or place.

examples.es: Habla con él para que se meta en el equipo.
examples.en: Talk to him so that he joins the team.
examples.note: Meterse en = to get into, to join.

contrast.es: Hablo con él para meterme en el equipo.
contrast.en: I'm talking to him to get into the team.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Meter is regular (meta, metas) and poner has -g- (ponga, pongas, pongamos). Check the destination: meter en is inside something and poner is on or at: 'que metas la llave en la cerradura' vs 'que pongas el libro sobre la mesa'. Meterse en also means to get involved: 'que no te metas'.

title: andar vs caminar

triggers.explanation: Calling something healthy is a judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es saludable que camines cada día.
examples.en: It's healthy that you walk every day.
examples.note: Caminar is the neutral verb for walking.

examples.es: Es saludable que andes un poco después de comer.
examples.en: It's healthy that you walk a little after eating.
examples.note: Andar is looser. The present subjunctive is regular: andes.

examples.es: Es saludable que caminemos más rápido.
examples.en: It's healthy that we walk faster.
examples.note: Nosotros form: caminemos.

contrast.es: Es evidente que caminamos más rápido.
contrast.en: It's obvious that we walk faster.
contrast.note: Es evidente states a fact (indicative). Es saludable judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Ojalá expresses a hope, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ojalá ande bien el reloj.
examples.en: I hope the watch works properly.
examples.note: Andar bien = to work well, for a machine.

examples.es: Ojalá no ande metido en problemas.
examples.en: I hope he isn't mixed up in trouble.
examples.note: Andar metido en = to be mixed up in.

examples.es: Ojalá ande mejor este coche.
examples.en: I hope this car runs better.
examples.note: Andar = to run, said of machines.

contrast.es: Este coche anda mejor.
contrast.en: This car runs better.
contrast.note: A statement of fact uses the indicative. A hope uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Saca al perro para que camine un rato.
examples.en: Take the dog out so that it walks for a while.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Dale la mano para que ande seguro.
examples.en: Hold his hand so that he walks safely.
examples.note: Andar seguro = to walk steadily.

examples.es: Sujétalo para que camine sin miedo.
examples.en: Hold him so that he walks without fear.
examples.note: A purpose with a different subject.

contrast.es: Camina sin miedo porque lo sujetas.
contrast.en: He walks without fear because you hold him.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Both are regular in the present subjunctive (ande, andes, camine, caminemos). The irregular anduve-type forms belong to the past, so don't carry them over. Caminar is neutral walking, while andar is looser and extends to machines and states: 'que ande bien' (that it works), 'que ande por ahí' (that he's around).

title: comprender vs entender

triggers.explanation: Hoping for something involves a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Espero que lo entiendas.
examples.en: I hope you understand it.
examples.note: Entender has e→ie: entiendas.

examples.es: Espero que comprendas mi situación.
examples.en: I hope you understand my situation.
examples.note: Comprender is regular, and slightly more formal.

examples.es: Espero que comprendas lo que siento.
examples.en: I hope you understand what I feel.
examples.note: Comprender = to grasp, even to sympathise.

contrast.es: Sé que comprendes lo que siento.
contrast.en: I know you understand what I feel.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Esperar expresses a hope (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Es difícil que means 'it's unlikely that': it's about probability, not fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Es difícil que entienda esto.
examples.en: He's unlikely to understand this.
examples.note: Es difícil que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Es difícil que entendamos todo.
examples.en: We're unlikely to understand everything.
examples.note: Nosotros keeps the e: entendamos.

examples.es: Es difícil que entiendan sus motivos.
