examples.en: They're unlikely to understand his motives.
examples.note: Ellos form: entiendan.

contrast.es: Es cierto que entienden sus motivos.
contrast.en: It's true that they understand his motives.
contrast.note: Es cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Es difícil judges it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Habla despacio para que te entienda.
examples.en: Speak slowly so that he understands you.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Explícalo con ejemplos para que lo comprendan.
examples.en: Explain it with examples so that they understand it.
examples.note: Comprender = to grasp.

examples.es: Escribe claro para que se comprenda.
examples.en: Write clearly so that it can be understood.
examples.note: Se comprenda = it can be understood.

contrast.es: Escribo claro porque se comprende mejor.
contrast.en: I write clearly because it's understood better.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Entender has e→ie (entienda, entiendan) but entendamos in nosotros; comprender is regular (comprenda). They're often interchangeable, but comprender is more formal or emotional ('que me comprendas' can mean sympathise). Don't slip into 'comprar': 'compre' is buy.

title: discutir vs comentar

triggers.explanation: Disliking something is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No me gusta que discutas con tu madre.
examples.en: I don't like you arguing with your mother.
examples.note: Discutir = to argue.

examples.es: No me gusta que comentes mi vida.
examples.en: I don't like you commenting on my life.
examples.note: Comentar = to comment on, to talk about.

examples.es: No me gusta que discutan delante de los niños.
examples.en: I don't like them arguing in front of the children.
examples.note: Discutir = to argue (in everyday speech).

contrast.es: Sé que discuten delante de los niños.
contrast.en: I know they argue in front of the children.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). No me gusta que reacts (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Llama a todos para que comenten el plan.
examples.en: Call everyone so that they comment on the plan.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Cálmate para que no discutamos.
examples.en: Calm down so that we don't argue.
examples.note: Nosotros form: discutamos.

examples.es: Llámame para que comentemos el contrato.
examples.en: Call me so that we can talk through the contract.
examples.note: Comentar = to talk over. Discutir would sound like a fight.

contrast.es: Llámame para comentar el contrato.
contrast.en: Call me to talk through the contract.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando discutas, no grites.
examples.en: When you argue, don't shout.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando comente la noticia, escucha.
examples.en: When he comments on the news, listen.
examples.note: Comentar la noticia = to talk about the news.

examples.es: Cuando discutamos, no te vayas.
examples.en: When we argue, don't leave.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando discutimos, te vas.
contrast.en: Whenever we argue, you leave.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Discutir is mostly a false friend: it usually means to argue (discuta), not to discuss. It can mean to debate a topic formally ('discutir un proyecto'), but for an everyday chat use comentar, hablar de or debatir. 'Que discutamos el contrato' can sound like a fight. Both verbs are regular.

title: tratar vs tratarse

triggers.explanation: Doubt means you don't take the statement as fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudo que trate bien a sus empleados.
examples.en: I doubt he treats his employees well.
examples.note: Tratar a = to treat someone.

examples.es: Dudo que se trate de algo grave.
examples.en: I doubt it's about anything serious.
examples.note: Tratarse de = to be about. Always singular: se trate.

examples.es: Dudo que trate de ayudarnos.
examples.en: I doubt he's trying to help us.
examples.note: Tratar de + infinitive = to try to.

contrast.es: No dudo que trata de ayudarnos.
contrast.en: I don't doubt he's trying to help us.
contrast.note: Dudar takes the subjunctive. No dudar expresses certainty, so the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Puede que expresses possibility, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Puede que trate de venir.
examples.en: He may try to come.
examples.note: Tratar de = to try.

examples.es: Puede que se trate de un error.
examples.en: It may be a mistake.
examples.note: Tratarse de + noun = to be a matter of.

examples.es: Puede que se trate de ti.
examples.en: It may be about you.
examples.note: Tratarse de is impersonal.

contrast.es: Seguro que se trata de ti.
contrast.en: It's surely about you.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Puede que = possibility (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando trates con él, sé amable.
examples.en: When you deal with him, be kind.
examples.note: Tratar con = to deal with.

examples.es: Cuando se trate de dinero, pídeme consejo.
examples.en: When it comes to money, ask me for advice.
examples.note: Tratarse de = to be a matter of.

examples.es: Cuando se trate de ti, seré justo.
examples.en: When it comes to you, I'll be fair.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando se trata de ti, soy justo.
contrast.en: Whenever it comes to you, I'm fair.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Tratar de + infinitive means to try, tratar a means to treat, tratar con means to deal with, and tratarse de means to be about. Tratarse de is impersonal and always singular: 'puede que se trate de unos ladrones', never 'se traten'. All are regular (trate, trates).

title: dedicar vs dedicarse

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quiero que dediques tiempo a tu familia.
examples.en: I want you to devote time to your family.
examples.note: Dedicar needs c→qu before e: dediques, never 'dedices'.

examples.es: Quiero que te dediques a la música.
examples.en: I want you to dedicate yourself to music.
examples.note: Dedicarse a = to devote yourself to, or to work in.

examples.es: Quiero que dediques este libro a tu madre.
examples.en: I want you to dedicate this book to your mother.
examples.note: Dedicar algo a alguien = to dedicate something to someone.

contrast.es: Sé que dedicas este libro a tu madre.
contrast.en: I know you dedicate this book to your mother.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Querer expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: A possibility isn't a fact, so the subjunctive is needed.

examples.es: Es posible que se dedique a la política.
examples.en: It's possible he works in politics.
examples.note: Dedicarse a = to work in a field.

examples.es: Es posible que dediquemos el verano a viajar.
examples.en: It's possible we'll spend the summer travelling.
examples.note: Dedicar el verano a + infinitive = to spend the summer on.

examples.es: Es posible que se dedique a vender coches.
examples.en: It's possible he sells cars for a living.
examples.note: Dedicarse a + infinitive = to do for a living.

contrast.es: Seguro que se dedica a vender coches.
contrast.en: I'm sure he sells cars for a living.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Es posible que = possibility (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando dediques tiempo a estudiar, aprobarás.
examples.en: When you devote time to studying, you'll pass.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando se dedique a pintar, será feliz.
examples.en: When he devotes himself to painting, he'll be happy.
examples.note: Dedicarse a + infinitive.

examples.es: Cuando me dedique a lo que amo, seré feliz.
examples.en: When I devote myself to what I love, I'll be happy.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando me dedico a lo que amo, soy feliz.
contrast.en: Whenever I devote myself to what I love, I'm happy.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Dedicar needs c→qu before e: dedique, dediques, dediquemos, never 'dedice'. Dedicarse a always takes a, as in '¿A qué te dedicas?' and 'que te dediques a la música'. Dedicar is to devote or dedicate something: 'que dediques tiempo a...'.

title: hay que vs tener que

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que haya que pagar.
examples.en: I don't think you have to pay.
examples.note: Hay que becomes haya que. It's impersonal and never changes.

examples.es: No creo que tengamos que esperar.
examples.en: I don't think we have to wait.
examples.note: Tener que changes with the person: tengamos.

examples.es: No creo que haya que tener tanto cuidado.
examples.en: I don't think you need to be that careful.
examples.note: Haya que + infinitive = one has to.

contrast.es: Creo que hay que tener tanto cuidado.
contrast.en: I think you need to be that careful.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Puede que expresses possibility, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Puede que tenga que irme.
examples.en: I may have to go.
examples.note: Tener que + infinitive = to have to.

examples.es: Puede que haya que repetirlo.
examples.en: We may have to repeat it.
examples.note: Impersonal haya que: no subject.

examples.es: Puede que tengas que pedirlo tú.
examples.en: You may have to ask for it yourself.
examples.note: Tener que points at a specific person.

contrast.es: Seguro que tienes que pedirlo tú.
contrast.en: You definitely have to ask for it yourself.
contrast.note: Seguro que = certainty (indicative). Puede que = possibility (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando tengas que irte, avísame.
examples.en: When you have to leave, let me know.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando haya que decidir, decidiremos.
examples.en: When it comes to deciding, we'll decide.
examples.note: Haya que + infinitive.

examples.es: Cuando tenga que votar, votaré.
examples.en: When I have to vote, I'll vote.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando tengo que votar, voto.
contrast.en: Whenever I have to vote, I vote.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Hay que is impersonal, so its subjunctive is just haya que, never 'hayan que' or 'haiga que': 'es posible que haya que esperar'. Tener que changes with the person (tenga, tengas, tengamos). The negatives differ in meaning: 'no hay que' usually means you mustn't (though it can also mean there's no need), while 'no tienes que' means you don't have to.

title: aprobar vs suspender

triggers.explanation: Hoping for something involves a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Espero que apruebes el examen.
examples.en: I hope you pass the exam.
examples.note: Aprobar has o→ue: apruebes. Aprobar = to pass an exam (pasar un examen is also heard, especially in Latin America).

examples.es: Espero que no suspendamos otra vez.
examples.en: I hope we don't fail again.
examples.note: Suspender = to fail in Spain. In much of Latin America: reprobar.

examples.es: Espero que no suspendan a tantos alumnos.
examples.en: I hope they don't fail so many students.
examples.note: Suspender a = to fail someone.

contrast.es: Sé que suspenden a tantos alumnos.
contrast.en: I know they fail so many students.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Esperar expresses a hope (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creo que apruebe sin estudiar.
examples.en: I don't think he'll pass without studying.
examples.note: Aprobar = to pass an exam.

examples.es: No creo que suspendan a nadie.
examples.en: I don't think they'll fail anybody.
examples.note: Suspender is regular: suspendan.

examples.es: No creo que suspenda el examen.
examples.en: I don't think she'll fail the exam.
examples.note: Suspender un examen = to fail an exam.

contrast.es: Creo que suspende el examen.
contrast.en: I think she fails the exam.
contrast.note: Creo que takes the indicative. No creo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Ayúdale a estudiar para que apruebe.
examples.en: Help him study so that he passes.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Repasa con ellos para que no suspendan.
examples.en: Revise with them so that they don't fail.
examples.note: Regular: suspendan.

examples.es: Dale clases para que apruebe el examen.
examples.en: Give him lessons so that he passes the exam.
examples.note: Purpose with a different subject.

contrast.es: Estudio para aprobar el examen.
contrast.en: I'm studying to pass the exam.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Aprobar has an o→ue change (apruebe, aprueben) but aprobemos in nosotros, and suspender is regular (suspenda). In English you 'pass' an exam; in Spanish the standard verb is aprobar (pasar is also heard, especially in Latin America). Suspender means to fail (Spain), and also to suspend or postpone; in much of Latin America, reprobar is used for fail.

title: caber

triggers.explanation: Fear is an emotion, and the thing feared hasn't happened, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Temo que no quepamos todos.
examples.en: I'm afraid we won't all fit.
examples.note: Caber is irregular: quepamos, from quepo.

examples.es: Temo que no quepa en el maletero.
examples.en: I'm afraid it won't fit in the boot.
examples.note: Caber en = to fit in. Maletero in Spain; cajuela in Mexico.

examples.es: Temo que no quepan todos los libros en la estantería.
examples.en: I'm afraid not all the books will fit on the shelf.
examples.note: Plural subject, so quepan.

contrast.es: Sé que no caben todos los libros en la estantería.
contrast.en: I know not all the books fit on the shelf.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative caben). Temer expresses fear (subjunctive quepan).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Mueve la mesa para que quepa el sofá.
examples.en: Move the table so that the sofa fits.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Compra una caja grande para que quepan los juguetes.
examples.en: Buy a big box so that the toys fit.
examples.note: Los juguetes is plural, so quepan.

examples.es: Aprieta un poco para que quepa todo.
examples.en: Squeeze a little so that everything fits.
examples.note: A purpose with a different subject.

contrast.es: Aprieto un poco porque no cabe todo.
contrast.en: I'm squeezing a little because not everything fits.
contrast.note: Porque (reason) takes the indicative. Para que (purpose) takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando quepas en ese vestido, lo compraremos.
examples.en: When you fit into that dress, we'll buy it.
examples.note: Future event, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Cuando quepan todos, saldremos.
examples.en: When everyone fits, we'll set off.
examples.note: Ellos form: quepan.

examples.es: Cuando no quepa más gente, cerraremos la puerta.
examples.en: When there's no more room, we'll close the door.
examples.note: A future event, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Cuando no cabe más gente, cierran la puerta.
contrast.en: Whenever there's no more room, they close the door.
contrast.note: A habit uses the indicative. A future event uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Caber is irregular: quepa, quepas, quepamos, quepan (built on quepo), never 'caba' or 'cabe'. It goes with en ('que quepa en el coche'), and the idiom 'no cabe duda de que' takes the indicative.

title: disfrutar vs gozar

triggers.explanation: Wishing something for someone is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te deseo que disfrutes mucho.
examples.en: I hope you enjoy yourself a lot.
examples.note: Disfrutar is regular: disfrutes.

examples.es: Te deseo que goces de buena salud.
examples.en: I wish you good health.
examples.note: Gozar de = to enjoy, formally. Z→c before e: goces.

examples.es: Te deseo que disfrutes de cada momento.
examples.en: I hope you enjoy every moment.
examples.note: Disfrutar de = to enjoy.

contrast.es: Sé que disfrutas de cada momento.
contrast.en: I know you enjoy every moment.
contrast.note: Sé que states a fact (indicative). Desear expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Pleasure at something is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me alegra que disfrutes del viaje.
examples.en: I'm glad you're enjoying the trip.
examples.note: Disfrutar de + noun.

examples.es: Me alegra que gocen de buena salud.
examples.en: I'm glad they enjoy good health.
examples.note: Gozar de buena salud = to be in good health.

examples.es: Me alegra que disfrutes de tu trabajo.
examples.en: I'm glad you enjoy your job.
examples.note: A reaction to a fact.

contrast.es: Veo que disfrutas de tu trabajo.
contrast.en: I see you enjoy your job.
contrast.note: Veo que states a fact (indicative). Me alegra que reacts (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Toca música para que disfruten los invitados.
examples.en: Play music so that the guests enjoy themselves.
examples.note: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Ahorra para que tus padres gocen de su jubilación.
examples.en: Save so that your parents enjoy their retirement.
examples.note: Gozar de = to enjoy the benefits of.

examples.es: Organiza una fiesta para que disfrutemos todos.
examples.en: Organise a party so that we can all enjoy ourselves.
examples.note: A purpose with a different subject.

contrast.es: Organizo una fiesta para disfrutar.
contrast.en: I'm organising a party to enjoy myself.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + subjunctive.

tricky: Disfrutar is regular (disfrute) and works with or without de ('disfruta la cena' or 'disfruta de la cena'). Gozar needs z→c: goce, goces, gocemos, never 'goze'. Gozar de is formal or literary ('gozar de buena salud'), and in some contexts it has a sexual sense, so disfrutar is the safe everyday choice.
